docs.title: 11.11.1. src/business/dates.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// business/dates.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Today's date in the "yyyy-MM-dd" format (that of the appointments.day column).
// It is used by BUSINESS RULES (no booking in the past, only one
// UPCOMING appointment per patient): it therefore lives in the business
// layer. The web layer reuses it (see web/helpers/dates.helper.ts).
//
// Two "yyyy-MM-dd" dates can be compared directly as strings:
// "2026-09-23" < "2026-10-01" - alphabetical order is chronological order.
// =========================================================================

// today's date, in the server's time zone
export function today(): string {
  const d = new Date();
  const twoDigits = (n: number) => n.toString().padStart(2, '0');
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${twoDigits(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${twoDigits(d.getDate())}`;
}

Lines 14–18: Today’s date in the format [yyyy-mm-dd]; the date in column [appointments.day]. [padStart(2, '0')] is used to pad a two-digit number (9 becomes [09]). In this format, alphabetical order is chronological order: two dates are compared using [<].

docs.title: 11.11.2. src/business/business.exception.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// business/business.exception.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The exception thrown by the business layer when a BUSINESS RULE is
// violated (login already taken, doctor who still has appointments, slot
// already booked...). It does not carry a text, but a translation
// KEY (e.g. 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'): it is the web layer that will
// translate it into French or English when displaying the page
// (see i18n/fr.json, i18n/en.json).
//
// The business layer thus remains independent of the interface language -
// as it was already independent of the output format (JSON or HTML).
// =========================================================================

export class BusinessException extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly key: string, // translation key of the message
    public readonly params: Record<string, string> = {}, // optional parameters of the message
  ) {
    super(key);
    this.name = 'BusinessException';
  }
}
  • line 17: a [BusinessException] does not carry a message, but a translation key ([ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN]). The business layer thus ignores the interface language: the view will translate the key (see Chapter 5);
  • line 18: any message parameters;
  • line 21: the exception name, displayed in error logs.

docs.title: 11.11.3. src/business/business.interface.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// business/business.interface.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The contract of the business layer. To the 11 methods of the JSON server (reading
// lists, schedule, adding/deleting an appointment) are added 2
// methods for the patient area and 6 methods to manage doctors
// and clients.
// =========================================================================

import { Client } from '../entities/client.entity';
import { Slot } from '../entities/slot.entity';
import { Doctor } from '../entities/doctor.entity';
import { Appointment } from '../entities/appointment.entity';
import { DoctorDaySchedule } from '../domain/doctor-day-schedule';

// the data entered in the "doctor" or "client" form
export interface PersonData {
  title: string; // Mr, Mme, Melle
  lastName: string;
  firstName: string;
  // creation: optional, defaults to the last name in lower case
  // update: optional, the login is unchanged if absent
  login?: string;
  // creation: optional, defaults to the login
  // update: optional, the password is unchanged if absent
  password?: string;
  // update: the version of the record when the form was
  // displayed (optimistic lock, see AbstractEntity.version)
  version?: number;
}

export interface IBusiness {
  // ------------------------------------------------ reads (unchanged)
  getAllClients(): Promise<Client[]>;
  getAllDoctors(): Promise<Doctor[]>;
  getAllSlots(doctorId: number): Promise<Slot[]>;
  getDoctorDayAppointments(doctorId: number, day: string): Promise<Appointment[]>;
  getClientById(id: number): Promise<Client | null>;
  getDoctorById(id: number): Promise<Doctor | null>;
  getAppointmentById(id: number): Promise<Appointment | null>;
  getSlotById(id: number): Promise<Slot | null>;
  getDoctorDaySchedule(doctorId: number, day: string): Promise<DoctorDaySchedule | null>;
  /** the client (patient) whose user account is [userId], or null */
  getClientByUserId(userId: number): Promise<Client | null>;
  /** the appointments of a client, today or in the future, with slot and doctor */
  getClientUpcomingAppointments(clientId: number): Promise<Appointment[]>;

  // ------------------------------------------------ appointments (ADMIN, DOCTOR, USER)
  /**
   * throws a BusinessException if:
   *  - the day is in the past ('ERRORS.PAST_DATE');
   *  - the patient already has an upcoming appointment ('ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT');
   *  - the slot is already taken that day ('ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED').
   */
  addAppointment(day: string, slot: Slot, client: Client): Promise<Appointment>;
  deleteAppointment(appointment: Appointment): Promise<void>;

  // ------------------------------------------------ doctors (ADMIN)
  /** creates the doctor AND the doctor's user account (role DOCTOR) */
  addDoctor(data: PersonData): Promise<Doctor>;
  /** updates the doctor AND the doctor's user account */
  editDoctor(id: number, data: PersonData): Promise<Doctor>;
  /** deletes the doctor, the slots AND the account - refused if there are appointments */
  deleteDoctor(id: number): Promise<void>;

  // ------------------------------------------------ clients
  // (the ADMIN; addClient is also used for a patient's registration,
  // editClient and deleteClient by the patient for their own account)
  /** creates the client AND the client's user account (role USER) */
  addClient(data: PersonData): Promise<Client>;
  editClient(id: number, data: PersonData): Promise<Client>;
  /**
   * deletes the client, the account AND all the appointments (past and future).
   * Used by the ADMIN ("Clients" page) and by the patient themselves
   * ("Manage my account").
   */
  deleteClient(id: number): Promise<void>;
}

export const BUSINESS_TOKEN = 'IBusiness';

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// business/business.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Implementation of the business layer.
//
// The reads and the schedule are taken as is from the JSON server. The
// new feature is the management of doctors and clients, which obeys three
// business rules:
//
//   1. a person (doctor or client) and their user account ALWAYS go
//      together: they are created, updated and deleted together, in
//      a single TRANSACTION - either everything succeeds, or nothing is written;
//   2. the login is unique across the whole application, and two doctors (or
//      two clients) cannot have the same first and last names;
//   3. deletion:
//      - a DOCTOR who has appointments cannot be deleted (the doctor's
//        patients would lose their appointment without being told): they
//        must be cancelled first. The doctor's time slots disappear too;
//      - a CLIENT, on the other hand, disappears with ALL their appointments (past and
//        future) - whether the deletion comes from the ADMIN or from the patient
//        themselves.
//
// And two rules for booking appointments, whatever the role of
// the person booking (ADMIN, DOCTOR or the patient themselves):
//   4. no appointment in the past;
//   5. a patient has only ONE upcoming appointment at a time.
//
// Doctors and clients follow exactly the same rules: the common code
// is written ONCE (private xxxPerson methods), and parameterized by a
// small "descriptor" that tells which type of person we are dealing with.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { DataSource, EntityManager, QueryFailedError } from 'typeorm';
import * as bcrypt from 'bcryptjs';
import { PersonData, IBusiness } from './business.interface';
import { BusinessException } from './business.exception';
import { DoctorRepository } from '../repositories/doctor.repository';
import { ClientRepository } from '../repositories/client.repository';
import { SlotRepository } from '../repositories/slot.repository';
import { AppointmentRepository } from '../repositories/appointment.repository';
import { UserRepository } from '../repositories/user.repository';
import { Client } from '../entities/client.entity';
import { Slot } from '../entities/slot.entity';
import { Doctor } from '../entities/doctor.entity';
import { Person } from '../entities/person.entity';
import { Appointment } from '../entities/appointment.entity';
import { Role, User } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { DoctorDaySchedule } from '../domain/doctor-day-schedule';
import { DoctorDaySlot } from '../domain/doctor-day-slot';
import { today } from './dates';

// number of bcrypt salt rounds - the same as in the SQL script ($2b$10$...)
const BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 10;

// what the two DAOs DoctorRepository and ClientRepository have in common
// (TypeScript checks compatibility by the SHAPE of objects: both
// classes satisfy this interface without having to declare it)
interface PersonDao<T extends Person> {
  findById(id: number, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<T | null>;
  findByFirstNameLastName(firstName: string, lastName: string, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<T | null>;
  save(person: T, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<T>;
  deleteById(id: number, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<void>;
}

// everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client for the business rules
interface PersonDescriptor<T extends Person> {
  dao: PersonDao<T>;
  create: () => T; // new Doctor() or new Client()
  role: Role; // DOCTOR or USER
  notFoundKey: string; // message if the person does not exist
  alreadyExistsKey: string; // message if the same first and last names already exist
  // optional: if present, deletion is REFUSED as long as the person
  // has appointments (countAppointments > 0), with the message hasAppointmentsKey
  countAppointments?: (id: number, manager: EntityManager) => Promise<number>;
  hasAppointmentsKey?: string;
  // optional: what must be deleted BEFORE the person (the rows that
  // reference the person through a foreign key)
  beforeDelete?: (id: number, manager: EntityManager) => Promise<void>;
}

@Injectable()
export class BusinessService implements IBusiness {
  private readonly doctorDescriptor: PersonDescriptor<Doctor>;
  private readonly clientDescriptor: PersonDescriptor<Client>;

  constructor(
    // DataSource: the TypeORM connection itself, provided by
    // TypeOrmModule.forRoot(...). We use it ONLY to open
    // transactions (dataSource.transaction(...)) - the queries, on the other hand,
    // remain in the DAO layer.
    private readonly dataSource: DataSource,
    private readonly doctorRepository: DoctorRepository,
    private readonly clientRepository: ClientRepository,
    private readonly slotRepository: SlotRepository,
    private readonly appointmentRepository: AppointmentRepository,
    private readonly userRepository: UserRepository,
  ) {
    this.doctorDescriptor = {
      dao: doctorRepository,
      create: () => new Doctor(),
      role: 'DOCTOR',
      notFoundKey: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND',
      alreadyExistsKey: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
      countAppointments: (id, manager) => appointmentRepository.countByDoctor(id, manager),
      hasAppointmentsKey: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS',
      // a doctor without appointments may still have time slots:
      // they make no sense without the doctor, they are deleted too (otherwise
      // the foreign key slots.doctor_id would forbid the deletion).
      beforeDelete: (id, manager) => slotRepository.deleteByDoctor(id, manager),
    };
    this.clientDescriptor = {
      dao: clientRepository,
      create: () => new Client(),
      role: 'USER',
      notFoundKey: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND',
      alreadyExistsKey: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
      // no countAppointments: deleting a client is never refused;
      // their appointments (past and future) are deleted with them (otherwise
      // the foreign key appointments.client_id would forbid the deletion)
      beforeDelete: (id, manager) => appointmentRepository.deleteByClient(id, manager),
    };
  }

  // =======================================================================
  // reads - unchanged compared with the JSON server
  // =======================================================================

  getAllClients(): Promise<Client[]> {
    return this.clientRepository.findAll();
  }

  getAllDoctors(): Promise<Doctor[]> {
    return this.doctorRepository.findAll();
  }

  getAllSlots(doctorId: number): Promise<Slot[]> {
    return this.slotRepository.getAllSlots(doctorId);
  }

  getDoctorDayAppointments(doctorId: number, day: string): Promise<Appointment[]> {
    return this.appointmentRepository.getDoctorDayAppointments(doctorId, day);
  }

  getClientById(id: number): Promise<Client | null> {
    return this.clientRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getDoctorById(id: number): Promise<Doctor | null> {
    return this.doctorRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getAppointmentById(id: number): Promise<Appointment | null> {
    return this.appointmentRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getSlotById(id: number): Promise<Slot | null> {
    return this.slotRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getClientByUserId(userId: number): Promise<Client | null> {
    return this.clientRepository.findByUserId(userId);
  }

  getClientUpcomingAppointments(clientId: number): Promise<Appointment[]> {
    return this.appointmentRepository.findUpcomingByClient(clientId, today());
  }

  // same algorithm as the JSON server (and as the original Spring project)
  async getDoctorDaySchedule(doctorId: number, day: string): Promise<DoctorDaySchedule | null> {
    const doctor = await this.getDoctorById(doctorId);
    if (doctor === null) {
      return null;
    }
    const timeSlots = await this.getAllSlots(doctorId);
    const bookings = await this.getDoctorDayAppointments(doctorId, day);
    const bookingsBySlot = new Map<number, Appointment>();
    for (const booking of bookings) {
      bookingsBySlot.set(booking.slotId, booking);
    }
    const doctorDaySlots = timeSlots.map(
      (slot) => new DoctorDaySlot(slot, bookingsBySlot.get(slot.id) ?? null),
    );
    return new DoctorDaySchedule(doctor, day, doctorDaySlots);
  }

  // =======================================================================
  // appointments
  // =======================================================================

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // booking an appointment, in a transaction:
  //   1. no appointment in the past;
  //   2. we LOCK the patient's row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE): if the
  //      same patient books two slots at the same moment (two tabs,
  //      double click...), the second transaction waits for the end of the
  //      first one - and then sees the appointment it has just created;
  //   3. only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  //   4. finally the insertion. If the slot has just been taken by ANOTHER
  //      patient, it is the SQL constraint unq1_appointments (day, slot_id) that
  //      refuses the insertion - translated into a BusinessException by transaction().
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  addAppointment(day: string, slot: Slot, client: Client): Promise<Appointment> {
    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      const todayDate = today();
      if (day < todayDate) {
        throw new BusinessException('ERRORS.PAST_DATE');
      }
      if ((await this.clientRepository.lock(client.id, manager)) === null) {
        throw new BusinessException('ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND');
      }
      if ((await this.appointmentRepository.countUpcomingByClient(client.id, todayDate, manager)) > 0) {
        throw new BusinessException('ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT');
      }
      const appointment = new Appointment();
      appointment.day = day;
      appointment.slot = slot;
      appointment.client = client;
      return this.appointmentRepository.save(appointment, manager);
    });
  }

  async deleteAppointment(appointment: Appointment): Promise<void> {
    await this.appointmentRepository.deleteById(appointment.id);
  }

  // =======================================================================
  // doctors and clients - the public methods delegate to the common
  // private methods, with the right descriptor
  // =======================================================================

  addDoctor(data: PersonData): Promise<Doctor> {
    return this.addPerson(this.doctorDescriptor, data);
  }

  editDoctor(id: number, data: PersonData): Promise<Doctor> {
    return this.editPerson(this.doctorDescriptor, id, data);
  }

  deleteDoctor(id: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.deletePerson(this.doctorDescriptor, id);
  }

  addClient(data: PersonData): Promise<Client> {
    return this.addPerson(this.clientDescriptor, data);
  }

  editClient(id: number, data: PersonData): Promise<Client> {
    return this.editPerson(this.clientDescriptor, id, data);
  }

  // the client, the account AND all the appointments (ADMIN, or the patient
  // themselves from "Manage my account": same method, same rule)
  deleteClient(id: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.deletePerson(this.clientDescriptor, id);
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // creation: the user account first (the person references it),
  // then the person - all in ONE transaction.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private addPerson<T extends Person>(d: PersonDescriptor<T>, data: PersonData): Promise<T> {
    const lastName = data.lastName.trim().toUpperCase();
    const firstName = data.firstName.trim();
    // the rules of the dbrdvmedecins2 database: login = last name in lower case,
    // password = login - unless the ADMIN entered other values
    const login = (data.login || lastName).toLowerCase();
    const password = data.password || login;

    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      await this.checkPersonUnique(d, firstName, lastName, null, manager);
      await this.checkLoginFree(login, manager);

      const user = new User();
      user.login = login;
      user.password = await bcrypt.hash(password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);
      user.name = `${firstName} ${lastName}`;
      user.role = d.role;
      await this.userRepository.save(user, manager);

      const person = d.create();
      person.title = data.title;
      person.lastName = lastName;
      person.firstName = firstName;
      person.user = user;
      return d.dao.save(person, manager);
    });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // update: the person AND the account (the display name "firstName LASTNAME"
  // must follow; the login and the password change only if they have been
  // entered).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private editPerson<T extends Person>(
    d: PersonDescriptor<T>,
    id: number,
    data: PersonData,
  ): Promise<T> {
    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      const person = await d.dao.findById(id, manager);
      if (person === null) {
        throw new BusinessException(d.notFoundKey);
      }
      // optimistic lock: if the version in the database is no longer that of the
      // form, someone has changed this record in the meantime - we refuse
      // rather than silently overwrite their changes.
      if (data.version !== undefined && data.version !== person.version) {
        throw new BusinessException('ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE');
      }

      person.title = data.title;
      person.lastName = data.lastName.trim().toUpperCase();
      person.firstName = data.firstName.trim();
      await this.checkPersonUnique(d, person.firstName, person.lastName, id, manager);

      const user = person.user;
      user.name = `${person.firstName} ${person.lastName}`;
      if (data.login && data.login.toLowerCase() !== user.login) {
        const login = data.login.toLowerCase();
        await this.checkLoginFree(login, manager);
        user.login = login;
      }
      if (data.password) {
        user.password = await bcrypt.hash(data.password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);
      }
      await this.userRepository.save(user, manager);
      return d.dao.save(person, manager);
    });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // deletion, in ONE transaction, in the order imposed by the foreign
  // keys:
  //   1. possible refusal if there are still appointments (doctor);
  //   2. what references the person (slots of a doctor, appointments
  //      of a client);
  //   3. the person (it references the account);
  //   4. the account.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private deletePerson<T extends Person>(d: PersonDescriptor<T>, id: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      const person = await d.dao.findById(id, manager);
      if (person === null) {
        throw new BusinessException(d.notFoundKey);
      }
      if (d.countAppointments && (await d.countAppointments(id, manager)) > 0) {
        throw new BusinessException(d.hasAppointmentsKey ?? 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM');
      }
      if (d.beforeDelete) {
        await d.beforeDelete(id, manager);
      }
      await d.dao.deleteById(id, manager);
      await this.userRepository.deleteById(person.userId, manager);
    });
  }

  // refuses a first and last name already used by ANOTHER person of the same type
  // (currentId: the person being updated, who obviously has the
  // right to keep their own first and last names; null for a creation)
  private async checkPersonUnique<T extends Person>(
    d: PersonDescriptor<T>,
    firstName: string,
    lastName: string,
    currentId: number | null,
    manager: EntityManager,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const namesake = await d.dao.findByFirstNameLastName(firstName, lastName, manager);
    if (namesake !== null && namesake.id !== currentId) {
      throw new BusinessException(d.alreadyExistsKey);
    }
  }

  private async checkLoginFree(login: string, manager: EntityManager): Promise<void> {
    if ((await this.userRepository.findByLogin(login, manager)) !== null) {
      throw new BusinessException('ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN');
    }
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // runs [work] in a transaction: dataSource.transaction() does
  // START TRANSACTION, calls [work] with an EntityManager bound to this
  // transaction, then COMMIT if everything went well - or ROLLBACK if an
  // exception was thrown (BusinessException included).
  //
  // The "login free" and "unique first + last name" checks are done BEFORE
  // the write, to give a clear message. But two ADMINs could
  // save the same login (or the same doctor) at the same moment: in that
  // rare case, it is an SQL uniqueness constraint that refuses the second
  // write - we then translate this SQL error into the same BusinessException.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private async transaction<R>(work: (manager: EntityManager) => Promise<R>): Promise<R> {
    try {
      return await this.dataSource.transaction(work);
    } catch (e) {
      throw translateDuplicate(e);
    }
  }
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Uniqueness constraint violations -> BusinessException
//
// When a UNIQUE constraint refuses a write, MySQL returns the error
// ER_DUP_ENTRY (no. 1062), whose message quotes the NAME of the constraint:
//   Duplicate entry 'marie-pelissier' for key 'doctors.unq_doctors_first_name_last_name'
// (MySQL 8 prefixes the name with the table's, MariaDB does not). That is
// why the SQL script NAMES all its constraints: each one can then
// be translated into its own message.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
const CONSTRAINT_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  unq_users_login: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN',
  unq_doctors_first_name_last_name: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
  unq_clients_first_name_last_name: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
  unq1_appointments: 'ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED',
};

// returns the BusinessException matching the violated constraint, or
// the original error, unchanged, if it is not a known violation
function translateDuplicate(e: unknown): unknown {
  if (!(e instanceof QueryFailedError)) {
    return e;
  }
  const sqlError = e.driverError as { code?: string; sqlMessage?: string };
  if (sqlError?.code !== 'ER_DUP_ENTRY') {
    return e;
  }
  // "... for key 'doctors.unq_doctors_first_name_last_name'" -> "unq_doctors_first_name_last_name"
  const constraint = /for key '(?:[^'.]*\.)?([^']+)'/.exec(sqlError.sqlMessage ?? e.message)?.[1];
  const key = constraint ? CONSTRAINT_MESSAGES[constraint] : undefined;
  return key ? new BusinessException(key) : e;
}

docs.title: 11.11.4.1. The descriptors
docs.text:
• line 54: the cost of bcrypt, the same as in the script SQL;
  • lines 59–64: what the DAO files for doctors and clients have in common. [TypeScript] compares types by their form: [DoctorRepository] and [ClientRepository] satisfy this interface without declaring it ([implements]);
  • Lines 67–80: Everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client in terms of business logic: its DAO, how to create an instance, the role of its account, its error messages, and what happens when it is deleted. Since doctors and clients follow the same rules, the code for these rules is written once, in generic methods parameterized by a descriptor;
  • lines 87–98: the constructor receives the [DataSource] (to open transactions) and the five DAO. It constructs the two descriptors. The one for doctors (lines 99–111) prevents the deletion of a doctor who has appointments ([countAppointments]) and deletes their time slots before the doctor is deleted ([beforeDelete]). The one for clients (lines 112–122) does not have a [countAppointments]: a client is deleted along with their appointments.

docs.title: 11.11.4.2. Read operations and the calendar
docs.text:
• lines 129–167: the queries delegate to the DAO layer;
  • lines 170–185: calendar calculation. The doctor’s time slots and today’s appointments are read; the appointments are stored in a [Map] indexed by their time slot ID; then each time slot is associated with its appointment, or with [null]. The [Map] avoids having to scan the list of appointments for each time slot.

docs.title: 11.11.4.3. Scheduling an appointment
docs.text:
• lines 203–221: everything takes place within a single transaction;
  • lines 206–208: no appointments in the past;
  • lines 209–211: the patient’s record is locked. Without this lock, two appointments for the same patient submitted at the same time (two tabs, a double-click) could both pass the following test before either one has written its appointment to the database. With the lock, the second transaction waits for the first to finish, then sees the appointment it created;
  • lines 212–214: only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  • lines 215–219: the insertion. If another patient has just booked the same time slot, the constraint [unq1_appointments] rejects the insertion, and the method [transaction] handles the error (see below);
  • lines 223–225: deleting an appointment.

docs.title: 11.11.4.4. Management of Doctors and Clients
docs.text:
• lines 232–256: the six public methods delegate to the three generic methods, using the correct descriptor;
  • Lines 262–288: Creation. The name is capitalized; by default, the username is the name in lowercase, and the password is the username (lines 267–268). Within the transaction: uniqueness rules are verified, the account is created (the password is hashed), followed by the person, who is linked to the account. If the second write operation fails, the first is rolled back: an account is never created without a person;
  • lines 295–299: the update. The optimistic lock (lines 308–310) rejects a record that has been modified in the meantime. The displayed name of the account follows the first name and last name; the username and password change only if they have been entered;
  • lines 341–356: deletion, in the order dictated by foreign keys: possible rejection (a doctor who has appointments), deletion of references to the person (a doctor’s time slots, a client’s appointments), deletion of the person, then deletion of their account;
  • lines 361–367: a person with the same name is rejected, unless it is the person themselves (modification);
  • lines 374–378: a username that is already taken is rejected.

docs.title: 11.11.4.5. Transactions and Uniqueness Constraints
docs.text:
• lines 392–398: All writes go through this method: [dataSource.transaction] commits or rolls back the transaction (see Example 28), and an error is translated by [translateDuplicate];
  • lines 411–416: each named uniqueness constraint in the SQL script has its own error message;
  • lines 420–432: an error SQL ([QueryFailedError]) with code [ER_DUP_ENTRY] is a uniqueness constraint violation. Its message includes the constraint name (prefixed by the table name with [MySQL] 8, without a prefix with [MariaDB]): the regular expression on line 429 extracts it. A known constraint becomes [BusinessException]; any other error is reported as-is: this is a genuine anomaly.

docs.title: 11.12.1. src/auth/auth.constants.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.constants.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Where does the JWT token travel?
//
// With the Angular client, it was the client's JavaScript code that kept
// the token (localStorage) and added it itself to each request (header
// "Authorization: Bearer ..."). A browser that displays ordinary HTML
// pages cannot do that: for it to present the token on its
// own with each request, the token must be stored in a COOKIE.
//
// The options of this cookie matter for security:
//   - httpOnly: the page's JavaScript cannot read the cookie (an
//     injected script could therefore not steal the token);
//   - sameSite 'lax': the browser does NOT send the cookie with a POST
//     coming from another site. As all the actions that change
//     data are POSTs, a booby-trapped page on another site cannot
//     book or delete anything by impersonating
//     the user (so-called CSRF attack);
//   - secure: in production (HTTPS), the cookie never travels in clear;
//   - maxAge: the cookie disappears at the same time as the token expires.
// =========================================================================

import { CookieOptions } from 'express';

export const COOKIE_JWT = 'rdvmedecins_jwt';

export const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET ?? 'dev-secret-change-in-production';

export const JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS = process.env.JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS
  ? parseInt(process.env.JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS, 10)
  : 7200;

export function jwtCookieOptions(): CookieOptions {
  return {
    httpOnly: true,
    sameSite: 'lax',
    secure: process.env.COOKIE_SECURE === 'true',
    maxAge: JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS * 1000, // in milliseconds for Express
    path: '/',
  };
}
  • lines 4–21: the comment explains why the token is stored in a cookie and the purpose of each of its options (see example 25);
  • line 28: the key, read from [.env]. The default value should only be used during development;
  • lines 30–32: the token’s lifetime: two hours by default;
  • lines 34–42: the cookie options, grouped in one place (they are used for logging in and modifying a patient’s account). [secure] is enabled only in production, where the site is served as HTTPS; [maxAge] is in milliseconds.

// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The authentication logic:
//   - validateUser() : checks a login / password pair;
//   - createToken()  : builds the JWT token of a validated user;
//   - readToken()    : checks a token (login page: if the
//                      user is already logged in, no need to ask
//                      for the password again).
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { JwtService } from '@nestjs/jwt';
import * as bcrypt from 'bcryptjs';
import { UserRepository } from '../repositories/user.repository';
import { User } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { JwtPayload } from './jwt.strategy';

@Injectable()
export class AuthService {
  constructor(
    private readonly userRepository: UserRepository,
    private readonly jwtService: JwtService,
  ) {}

  async validateUser(login: string, password: string): Promise<User | null> {
    const user = await this.userRepository.findByLogin(login);
    if (user === null) {
      return null;
    }
    return (await bcrypt.compare(password, user.password)) ? user : null;
  }

  createToken(user: User): string {
    const payload: JwtPayload = { sub: user.id, login: user.login, name: user.name, role: user.role };
    return this.jwtService.sign(payload);
  }

  // returns the content of the token if it is valid (correct signature, not
  // expired), null otherwise
  readToken(token: string | undefined): JwtPayload | null {
    if (!token) {
      return null;
    }
    try {
      return this.jwtService.verify<JwtPayload>(token);
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }
}
  • lines 26–32: the account if the username and password are correct ([bcrypt.compare]), [null] otherwise;
  • lines 34–37: the token, which contains the ID, username, display name, and role;
  • lines 41–50: [jwtService.verify] verifies a token’s signature and expiration date, and throws an exception if it is invalid. This method is used by unprotected pages (the login page) that want to determine whether the user is already logged in.

// =========================================================================
// auth/jwt.strategy.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The Passport strategy that authenticates EACH protected request from the
// JWT token. Only difference with the JSON server: the token is read from the
// [rdvmedecins_jwt] cookie (see auth.constants.ts) instead of the
// "Authorization: Bearer ..." header.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PassportStrategy } from '@nestjs/passport';
import { Request } from 'express';
import { ExtractJwt, Strategy } from 'passport-jwt';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { COOKIE_JWT, JWT_SECRET } from './auth.constants';

// what is stored IN the token when it is built (see AuthService).
// The display name is also there, so that the navigation bar can
// display it without querying the database on each page.
export interface JwtPayload {
  sub: number; // the user's id (JWT convention)
  login: string;
  name: string;
  role: Role;
}

// what request.user will contain once the token is verified
export interface ConnectedUser {
  userId: number;
  login: string;
  name: string;
  role: Role;
}

@Injectable()
export class JwtStrategy extends PassportStrategy(Strategy, 'jwt') {
  constructor() {
    super({
      // fromExtractors([...]): we provide OUR own token extraction
      // function - here, reading a cookie (req.cookies is filled by the
      // cookie-parser middleware, see main.ts).
      jwtFromRequest: ExtractJwt.fromExtractors([(req: Request) => req?.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT] ?? null]),
      ignoreExpiration: false,
      secretOrKey: JWT_SECRET,
    });
  }

  validate(payload: JwtPayload): ConnectedUser {
    return { userId: payload.sub, login: payload.login, name: payload.name, role: payload.role };
  }
}
  • lines 20–25: the token’s contents;
  • lines 28–33: what [req.user] will contain;
  • lines 38–45: the token is read from the cookie; if it has expired or is incorrectly signed, it is rejected;
  • lines 48–50: the token’s content becomes [req.user].

// =========================================================================
// auth/roles.decorator.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// @Roles('ADMIN') is a HOME-MADE decorator (we write it ourselves,
// unlike @Get/@Post/@Injectable provided by NestJS): it merely
// attaches a piece of metadata ("this method requires such a role") to
// the method it decorates, without checking anything itself - it is RolesGuard
// (see roles.guard.ts) that will read this metadata and perform the check.
//
// SetMetadata(key, value) is the low-level NestJS function that lets
// you write this kind of "custom" decorator: we use it here so as not to
// have to repeat the 'roles' string everywhere in the code.
// =========================================================================

import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';

export const ROLES_KEY = 'roles';
export const Roles = (...roles: Role[]) => SetMetadata(ROLES_KEY, roles);

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/roles.guard.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Second level of control, AFTER JwtAuthGuard: the latter only checks
// that we are indeed authenticated (a valid JWT token); RolesGuard
// additionally checks that the role of the logged-in user (request.user.role,
// set by JwtStrategy) is among those required by @Roles(...)
// on the targeted method.
//
// Unchanged compared with the JSON server, except the destination of the error:
// the ForbiddenException thrown here is turned into a "403 - access
// forbidden" PAGE by HtmlExceptionFilter (see web/html-exception.filter.ts).
//
// It is the equivalent, in spirit, of the Spring Security rule:
//   http.authorizeRequests().antMatchers(...).hasRole("ADMIN")
// but applied here method by method rather than URL by URL, thanks to the
// pair decorator (@Roles) + Reflector (which can read back the metadata
// set by a decorator).
// =========================================================================

import { CanActivate, ExecutionContext, ForbiddenException, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core';
import { ROLES_KEY } from './roles.decorator';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { ConnectedUser } from './jwt.strategy';

@Injectable()
export class RolesGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(private readonly reflector: Reflector) {}

  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
    // we read back the metadata set by @Roles(...) on the targeted method -
    // getAllAndOverride looks first on the method, then on the class.
    const requiredRoles = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<Role[]>(ROLES_KEY, [context.getHandler(), context.getClass()]);

    // no @Roles(...) metadata on this method: no additional role
    // restriction (JwtAuthGuard will already have required a valid
    // authentication, whatever the role).
    if (!requiredRoles || requiredRoles.length === 0) {
      return true;
    }

    // request.user was set by JwtStrategy.validate() (see jwt.strategy.ts) -
    // RolesGuard therefore ALWAYS runs after JwtAuthGuard (see their order
    // in @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard), see src/web/controllers/).
    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest<{ user: ConnectedUser }>();
    const user = request.user;

    if (!requiredRoles.includes(user.role)) {
      throw new ForbiddenException(
        `role [${user.role}] does not allow this action (required role: ${requiredRoles.join(', ')})`,
      );
    }
    return true;
  }
}

The role mapping is identical to that in Example 26.

// =========================================================================
// auth/captcha.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A CAPTCHA ("test to tell a human from a robot") built by the
// server itself, without any external service: the svg-captcha library
// draws a few distorted characters, blurred by lines, in an
// SVG image. A human reads them easily; a robot that just
// sends forms in a loop cannot.
//
// How it works:
//   1. generate() draws a random text, turns it into an image, and stores the
//      right answer IN THE SERVER'S MEMORY, under a random identifier;
//   2. the page displays the image and puts the identifier in a hidden field
//      of the form (the answer itself never leaves the server);
//   3. verify(id, input) compares the input with the expected answer, then
//      FORGETS this captcha: each image is used only once, a robot cannot
//      replay an answer already found.
//
// Accepted limit: the memory of a single Node process. With several
// servers behind a load balancer, a shared storage
// would be needed (Redis, database...).
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto';
import * as svgCaptcha from 'svg-captcha';

// validity of an image: you have 10 minutes to fill in the form
const LIFETIME_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;
// memory safeguard: beyond that, the oldest captchas are forgotten
const MAX_CAPTCHAS = 10_000;

export interface Captcha {
  id: string; // to put in the hidden "captchaId" field of the form
  svg: string; // the image, to insert as is in the page
}

@Injectable()
export class CaptchaService {
  // id -> { expected answer, expiry date }. A Map keeps the insertion
  // order: its first entries are the oldest ones.
  private readonly pending = new Map<string, { text: string; expires: number }>();

  generate(): Captcha {
    this.purge();
    const { text, data } = svgCaptcha.create({
      size: 5, // 5 characters
      noise: 3, // 3 blurring lines
      color: true,
      background: '#f5f7fa',
      // characters too easy to confuse with one another: excluded
      ignoreChars: '0oO1iIlL',
    });
    const id = randomUUID();
    this.pending.set(id, { text: text.toLowerCase(), expires: Date.now() + LIFETIME_MS });
    return { id, svg: data };
  }

  // true if [input] is the right answer to captcha [id] (regardless
  // of case). The captcha is consumed in every case.
  verify(id: unknown, input: unknown): boolean {
    if (typeof id !== 'string' || typeof input !== 'string') {
      return false;
    }
    const expected = this.pending.get(id);
    this.pending.delete(id);
    return expected !== undefined && expected.expires > Date.now() && expected.text === input.trim().toLowerCase();
  }

  private purge(): void {
    const now = Date.now();
    for (const [id, { expires }] of this.pending) {
      if (expires <= now || this.pending.size >= MAX_CAPTCHAS) {
        this.pending.delete(id);
      }
    }
  }
}
  • Lines 29–31: Compared to Example 27, a CAPTCHA has a lifespan (ten minutes), and the number of CAPTCHAs in memory is capped: a bot requesting the login page millions of times would not be able to exhaust the server’s memory;
  • line 42: a [Map] preserves the order of insertion: its earliest entries are the oldest;
  • lines 44–57: the image, its expected response (in lowercase), and its expiration date;
  • lines 61–68: The answer is compared without regard to case; the CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases;
  • lines 70–77: Expired CAPTCHAs are discarded, as are the oldest ones if the limit is reached.

// =========================================================================
// auth/attempt-limiter.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Second line of defence against bots (the first one is the captcha): we COUNT
// the attempts, and beyond a threshold we BLOCK for a while.
//
//   - login: after LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES failures (wrong captcha or wrong
//     password) for the same login from the same IP address, this pair
//     is blocked for LOGIN_BLOCK_MINUTES minutes. The same IP address is also
//     blocked if it accumulates 5 times more failures, all logins combined (a
//     bot that tries thousands of different logins);
//   - account creation: at most REGISTRATION_MAX_PER_HOUR accounts created
//     per hour from the same IP address.
//
// Beware in a classroom: all the computers often go out to the Internet
// through the SAME IP address. That is why the login block applies
// first to the (IP, login) pair - a student who mistypes their
// password does not block their neighbours - and why the thresholds can be set
// in the .env file.
//
// As for the captcha, the counters live in the memory of the process.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';

interface Counter {
  count: number; // attempts counted in the current window
  start: number; // start of the counting window (ms)
  blockedUntil: number; // 0 if not blocked
}

const MINUTE = 60 * 1000;

function envInteger(name: string, fallback: number): number {
  const value = parseInt(process.env[name] ?? '', 10);
  return Number.isInteger(value) && value > 0 ? value : fallback;
}

@Injectable()
export class AttemptLimiterService {
  private readonly counters = new Map<string, Counter>();

  private readonly maxLoginFailures = envInteger('LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES', 5);
  private readonly loginBlockDuration = envInteger('LOGIN_BLOCK_MINUTES', 15) * MINUTE;
  private readonly maxRegistrations = envInteger('REGISTRATION_MAX_PER_HOUR', 10);

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- login

  // number of remaining minutes of blocking (0 = the attempt is allowed)
  loginBlockMinutes(ip: string, login: string): number {
    return Math.max(this.remainingMinutes(loginKey(ip, login)), this.remainingMinutes(ipKey(ip)));
  }

  loginFailure(ip: string, login: string): void {
    this.count(loginKey(ip, login), this.maxLoginFailures, this.loginBlockDuration, this.loginBlockDuration);
    this.count(ipKey(ip), this.maxLoginFailures * 5, this.loginBlockDuration, this.loginBlockDuration);
  }

  // a successful login resets the counter of THIS login
  loginSuccess(ip: string, login: string): void {
    this.counters.delete(loginKey(ip, login));
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- registration

  registrationBlockMinutes(ip: string): number {
    return this.remainingMinutes(`registration|${ip}`);
  }

  registrationSuccess(ip: string): void {
    // one-hour window; once the quota is reached, blocked until the end of the hour
    this.count(`registration|${ip}`, this.maxRegistrations, 60 * MINUTE, 60 * MINUTE);
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- common mechanics

  private remainingMinutes(key: string): number {
    const c = this.counters.get(key);
    const remaining = c ? c.blockedUntil - Date.now() : 0;
    return remaining > 0 ? Math.ceil(remaining / MINUTE) : 0;
  }

  // counts an attempt; if the threshold is reached within the window, blocks
  private count(key: string, max: number, window: number, block: number): void {
    const now = Date.now();
    this.purge(now);
    let c = this.counters.get(key);
    if (!c || now - c.start > window) {
      c = { count: 0, start: now, blockedUntil: 0 };
      this.counters.set(key, c);
    }
    c.count++;
    if (c.count >= max) {
      c.blockedUntil = now + block;
      c.count = 0; // after the block, we start again from zero
      c.start = c.blockedUntil;
    }
  }

  // we forget the counters that are no longer useful (neither blocked, nor recent)
  private purge(now: number): void {
    if (this.counters.size < 1000) {
      return;
    }
    for (const [key, c] of this.counters) {
      if (c.blockedUntil < now && now - c.start > 60 * MINUTE) {
        this.counters.delete(key);
      }
    }
  }
}

function loginKey(ip: string, login: string): string {
  return `login|${ip}|${login.trim().toLowerCase()}`;
}

function ipKey(ip: string): string {
  return `ip|${ip}`;
}
  • lines 26–30: an attempt counter, with the start of its counting window and its lockout end date;
  • lines 34–37: a threshold read from [.env], with a default value;
  • lines 50–52: The lock applies to the pair (address IP, login), and to address IP alone when it accumulates a large number of failed attempts, across all logins. In a classroom, all workstations often connect via the same address, IP: a student who enters the wrong password should not lock out their neighbors;
  • lines 54–57: one failed attempt counts toward both keys;
  • lines 66–68 and 70–73: the number of accounts created per hour from the same address, IP, is limited;
  • lines 84–98: counting. An expired window resets to zero; when the threshold is reached, the key is blocked;
  • lines 101–110: clearing old counters to prevent keys from accumulating indefinitely in memory;
  • lines 113–118: generation of keys for [Map].

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/registration-pass.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The "pass" for account creation.
//
// To open the "Create a patient account" page, you must first have
// typed the captcha of the authentication page (see
// RegistrationController, POST /register/access). The server then
// issues a pass:
//   - a random identifier, stored in an httpOnly cookie;
//   - valid for 15 minutes (time to fill in the form, even when
//     trying several times after input errors);
//   - consumed as soon as an account is created: ONE solved captcha = ONE account at
//     most. A bot cannot create accounts in bulk.
//
// Without a valid pass, GET and POST /register send back to the
// authentication page: typing the /register URL directly does not
// get around the captcha.
//
// Like the captcha, the passes live in the memory of the process.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto';
import { CookieOptions } from 'express';

export const COOKIE_REGISTRATION_PASS = 'rdvmedecins_registration';

const LIFETIME_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;
const MAX_PASSES = 10_000;

@Injectable()
export class RegistrationPassService {
  // id -> expiry date
  private readonly passes = new Map<string, number>();

  // issues a new pass; returns its identifier
  issue(): string {
    this.purge();
    const id = randomUUID();
    this.passes.set(id, Date.now() + LIFETIME_MS);
    return id;
  }

  // true if [id] is an existing, non-expired pass
  isValid(id: unknown): boolean {
    if (typeof id !== 'string') {
      return false;
    }
    const expires = this.passes.get(id);
    return expires !== undefined && expires > Date.now();
  }

  // the pass has been used: we forget it
  consume(id: unknown): void {
    if (typeof id === 'string') {
      this.passes.delete(id);
    }
  }

  cookieOptions(): CookieOptions {
    return { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax', maxAge: LIFETIME_MS, path: '/register' };
  }

  private purge(): void {
    const now = Date.now();
    for (const [id, expires] of this.passes) {
      if (expires <= now || this.passes.size >= MAX_PASSES) {
        this.passes.delete(id);
      }
    }
  }
}

Creating a patient account is available from the login page, provided the CAPTCHA has been solved. Therefore, a request (the registration form) must know that a previous request solved the CAPTCHA. This is the role of the pass:

  • lines 38–43: a random identifier, valid for 15 minutes, stored in memory; it will be saved in a cookie;
  • lines 46–52: the registration form is displayed and accepted only with a valid pass;
  • lines 55–59: Creating an account consumes the pass: a solved CAPTCHA entitles the user to one account, and no more;
  • lines 61–63: The option [path: '/register'] restricts the sending of the cookie to URLs that begin with [/register].

docs.title: 11.12.10. src/auth/auth.controller.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The NON-protected login routes:
//   GET  /        redirects to the home page of the role (or to /login)
//   GET  /login   displays the login form (with its captcha)
//   POST /login   checks attempt limit, captcha, login / password
//   POST /logout  clears the token cookie
//
// The JSON server used a Passport "local" guard for POST /login:
// on failure, it answered 401 directly, which suits a
// JavaScript client. An HTML page, however, must DISPLAY the form AGAIN
// with an error message: so we call AuthService ourselves.
//
// Protection against bots, in this order (see captcha.service.ts and
// attempt-limiter.service.ts):
//   1. too many recent failures for this login from this IP address?
//      -> immediate refusal, without even looking at the password;
//   2. wrong answer to the captcha? -> refusal (counted as a failure);
//   3. only then, the password is checked.
// The password of an attempt refused at steps 1 or 2 is NEVER checked:
// a bot can therefore learn nothing by insisting.
// =========================================================================

import { Body, Controller, Get, HttpCode, Post, Query, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { AuthService } from './auth.service';
import { CaptchaService } from './captcha.service';
import { AttemptLimiterService } from './attempt-limiter.service';
import { COOKIE_JWT, jwtCookieOptions } from './auth.constants';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';

// the home page of each role, right after login
export function homePage(role: Role): string {
  return role === 'USER' ? '/my-area' : '/schedule';
}

@Controller()
export class AuthController {
  constructor(
    private readonly authService: AuthService,
    private readonly captchaService: CaptchaService,
    private readonly limiter: AttemptLimiterService,
  ) {}

  @Get()
  home(@Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response): void {
    const token = this.authService.readToken(req.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT]);
    res.redirect(token ? homePage(token.role) : '/login');
  }

  // GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the login
  // field (used right after an account is created, see RegistrationController)
  @Get('login')
  showLogin(@Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response, @Query('login') login?: string): void {
    // already logged in (token still valid): straight to the home page
    const token = this.authService.readToken(req.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT]);
    if (token !== null) {
      return res.redirect(homePage(token.role));
    }
    this.showForm(res, typeof login === 'string' ? login.slice(0, 30) : '');
  }

  // @HttpCode(200): by default, NestJS answers 201 (Created) to a POST - which
  // makes no sense when the form is DISPLAYED AGAIN (a redirect, for its part,
  // imposes its own code anyway, 302).
  @Post('login')
  @HttpCode(200)
  async logIn(
    @Body() body: { login?: string; password?: string; captchaId?: string; captcha?: string },
    @Req() req: Request,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const login = (body.login ?? '').trim();
    const password = body.password ?? '';
    const ip = req.ip ?? 'unknown';

    // 1. too many recent failures?
    const minutes = this.limiter.loginBlockMinutes(ip, login);
    if (minutes > 0) {
      return this.showForm(res, login, 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', { minutes: String(minutes) });
    }

    // 2. the captcha
    if (!this.captchaService.verify(body.captchaId, body.captcha)) {
      this.limiter.loginFailure(ip, login);
      return this.showForm(res, login, 'ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA');
    }

    // 3. the password
    const user = login && password ? await this.authService.validateUser(login, password) : null;
    if (user === null) {
      this.limiter.loginFailure(ip, login);
      return this.showForm(res, login, 'LOGIN.ERROR');
    }

    this.limiter.loginSuccess(ip, login);
    res.cookie(COOKIE_JWT, this.authService.createToken(user), jwtCookieOptions());
    res.redirect(homePage(user.role));
  }

  // logout with a POST (and not with a simple GET link): a third-party site
  // cannot log the user out without their knowledge (see sameSite, auth.constants.ts)
  @Post('logout')
  logOut(@Res() res: Response): void {
    res.clearCookie(COOKIE_JWT, { path: '/' });
    res.redirect('/login');
  }

  // the form, always with a NEW captcha (each image is used only once)
  private showForm(
    res: Response,
    login: string,
    error?: string,
    errorParams?: Record<string, string>,
  ): void {
    res.render('login', {
      pageTitle: 'LOGIN.TITLE',
      login, // the entered login is displayed again, never the password
      captcha: this.captchaService.generate(),
      error,
      errorParams,
    });
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 34–36: The home page depends on the user’s role: “My area” for patients, the calendar for everyone else;
  • lines 46–50: The site root redirects depending on whether the user is logged in or not. Since the route is not protected by the guard, the token is verified by [readToken];
  • lines 54–62: A user who is already logged in is sent to their home page. The parameter [login] pre-fills the field (after an account is created). [slice(0, 30)] limits its length: data from the request is never used without precautions;
  • lines 69–73: the login process, in order: potential lockout, CAPTCHA, then password (see Example 27). [req.ip] is the client’s IP address. If successful: counter reset to zero, cookie set, redirection to the role’s home page;
  • lines 104–108: logout;
  • lines 111–116: the login page, always with a new CAPTCHA. The error is a translation key, along with its parameters (the number of minutes of lockout).

// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.module.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The authentication module. It EXPORTS:
//   - UserRepository, which the business layer needs (create, update,
//     delete the account of a doctor or a client - see business.service.ts);
//   - AuthService, CaptchaService, AttemptLimiterService and
//     RegistrationPassService, also used by the "Create an account" pages
//     and "Manage my account" (src/web/).
// =========================================================================

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { JwtModule } from '@nestjs/jwt';
import { PassportModule } from '@nestjs/passport';
import { TypeOrmModule } from '@nestjs/typeorm';
import { User } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { UserRepository } from '../repositories/user.repository';
import { AuthService } from './auth.service';
import { AuthController } from './auth.controller';
import { JwtStrategy } from './jwt.strategy';
