docs.title: 11.13.1. src/web/i18n.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/i18n.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// French / English translation of the interface.
//
// The Angular client loaded its dictionaries (public/i18n/fr.json and
// en.json) in the BROWSER with @ngx-translate. Here, the pages are
// built on the SERVER: these are therefore the same dictionaries (same
// keys, completed), but read only once by the server at startup.
// A Handlebars view translates a key with the helper {{t 'KEY'}}
// (see views/handlebars-helpers.ts), the equivalent of the `| translate` pipe.
// =========================================================================

import { readFileSync } from 'fs';
import { join } from 'path';
import { I18N_DIR } from '../config/paths';

export type Language = 'fr' | 'en';
export const LANGUAGES: Language[] = ['fr', 'en'];
export const DEFAULT_LANGUAGE: Language = 'en';

// a dictionary is a nested JSON object: { "LOGIN": { "TITLE": "Login" } }
type Dictionary = { [key: string]: string | Dictionary };

const dictionaries: Record<Language, Dictionary> = {
  fr: JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(I18N_DIR, 'fr.json'), 'utf-8')),
  en: JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(I18N_DIR, 'en.json'), 'utf-8')),
};

export function isLanguage(value: unknown): value is Language {
  return typeof value === 'string' && (LANGUAGES as string[]).includes(value);
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// translate('en', 'DOCTORS.ADDED', { name: 'Marie PELISSIER' })
//   -> looks up DOCTORS then ADDED in the English dictionary, and replaces
//      {name} with its value. A key missing from the requested language is
//      looked up in the default language; missing everywhere, the key itself is shown
//      (an omission in the dictionaries is thus spotted immediately).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function translate(language: Language, key: string, params: Record<string, unknown> = {}): string {
  const text = lookup(dictionaries[language], key) ?? lookup(dictionaries[DEFAULT_LANGUAGE], key) ?? key;
  return text.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (whole, name: string) => (name in params ? String(params[name]) : whole));
}

function lookup(dictionary: Dictionary, key: string): string | null {
  let node: string | Dictionary | undefined = dictionary;
  for (const part of key.split('.')) {
    if (typeof node !== 'object' || node === null) {
      return null;
    }
    node = node[part];
  }
  return typeof node === 'string' ? node : null;
}

The translation module from Example 22, with one clarification (line 42): if a key is missing from the French dictionary, it is looked up in the English dictionary (the default language); if it is missing from both, the key itself is displayed.

docs.title: 11.13.2. src/web/view-context.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/view-context.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What ALL the pages need to know, whatever the route
// that displays them: the interface language, the possible "flash" message to
// display, and the logged-in user (for the navigation bar).
//
// Express offers [res.locals] for that: an object attached to the response, whose
// content is AUTOMATICALLY merged with the model of each view at the
// moment of res.render(...). The controllers therefore do not have to repeat this
// information in each of their models.
//
// Reminder: the Angular client kept this information in the browser
// (signals + localStorage). An HTML server, however, must find it again on
// EACH request - here in cookies.
// =========================================================================

import { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import { Language, DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, isLanguage } from './i18n';
import { ConnectedUser } from '../auth/jwt.strategy';

export const COOKIE_LANGUAGE = 'rdvmedecins_language';
export const COOKIE_FLASH = 'rdvmedecins_flash';

// a message to display ONCE, on the next page
export interface FlashMessage {
  type: 'success' | 'danger'; // Bootstrap classes alert-success / alert-danger
  key: string; // translation key
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

// the logged-in user, as the views see them
export interface ViewUser {
  login: string;
  name: string;
  role: string;
  isAdmin: boolean; // ADMIN: Doctors / Clients menus
  isPatient: boolean; // USER: My area menu
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Express middleware, run BEFORE any route (see main.ts):
//   - res.locals.lang  : chosen language (cookie), English by default;
//   - res.locals.flash : the possible flash message, which is cleared
//                        at once (it must be displayed only once);
//   - res.locals.currentPath: the requested URL (active menu of the navigation bar).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function viewContextMiddleware(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
  res.locals.lang = languageOf(req);
  res.locals.currentPath = req.path;
  res.locals.flash = null;
  res.locals.currentUser = null;

  const raw = req.cookies?.[COOKIE_FLASH];
  if (raw) {
    try {
      res.locals.flash = JSON.parse(raw) as FlashMessage;
    } catch {
      // unreadable cookie: ignored
    }
    res.clearCookie(COOKIE_FLASH);
  }
  next();
}

export function languageOf(req: Request): Language {
  const value = req.cookies?.[COOKIE_LANGUAGE];
  return isLanguage(value) ? value : DEFAULT_LANGUAGE;
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// sets a flash message, which will be displayed by the NEXT page. It is the
// natural complement of the "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern used by all the
// forms of the application: a successful POST does not build a page, it
// redirects (302) to a GET page - if the user then reloads this
// page (F5), the browser does not send the form a second time.
// The message, however, must survive the redirect: a short-lived
// cookie does the job.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function flash(res: Response, message: FlashMessage): void {
  res.cookie(COOKIE_FLASH, JSON.stringify(message), { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax', maxAge: 60_000 });
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// exposes the logged-in user (request.user, set by JwtStrategy) to the
// views. Called by ViewUserInterceptor (normal routes) and by
// HtmlExceptionFilter (error pages).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function exposeUser(req: Request, res: Response): void {
  const user = (req as Request & { user?: ConnectedUser }).user;
  if (!user) {
    return;
  }
  const currentUser: ViewUser = {
    login: user.login,
    name: user.name,
    role: user.role,
    isAdmin: user.role === 'ADMIN',
    isPatient: user.role === 'USER',
  };
  res.locals.currentUser = currentUser;
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 22–23: the names of the language and flash message cookies;
  • lines 26–30: a flash message: a type (success or error), a translation key, and its parameters. It is stored in the cookie as JSON;
  • lines 33–39: the logged-in user, as seen by the views. The booleans [isAdmin] and [isPatient] prevent the views from comparing strings;
  • lines 48–64: the middleware executed before any route (see examples 20 and 22): the language, the path (for the active menu), and the flash message, which is read and then cleared. [JSON.parse] is protected by a [try]: a manually modified cookie should not cause the page to fail;
  • lines 66–69: the language, based on its cookie;
  • lines 80–82: displays a flash message (see example 20);
  • Lines 89–102: Copies the logged-in user ([req.user]) to [res.locals] for the navigation bar. This function is not called by the middleware: the middleware runs before the guards, and therefore before [req.user] exists (see Chapter 7). It is called by the following interceptor and by the exception filter.

docs.title: 11.13.3. src/web/view-user.interceptor.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/view-user.interceptor.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Why an interceptor and not simply the middleware of
// view-context.ts? Because the execution ORDER matters:
//
//     middlewares -> guards (JwtAuthGuard...) -> interceptors -> controller
//
// It is the JwtAuthGuard guard that sets request.user: a middleware runs
// too early to see it. An interceptor, however, runs AFTER the guards and
// BEFORE the controller - the right moment to copy the logged-in user
// into res.locals, where all the views will find it.
// =========================================================================

import { CallHandler, ExecutionContext, Injectable, NestInterceptor } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { Observable } from 'rxjs';
import { exposeUser } from './view-context';

@Injectable()
export class ViewUserInterceptor implements NestInterceptor {
  intercept(context: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler): Observable<unknown> {
    const http = context.switchToHttp();
    exposeUser(http.getRequest<Request>(), http.getResponse<Response>());
    return next.handle();
  }
}

Lines 22–26: An interceptor runs after the guards and before the action: this is the right time to expose the user passed by [JwtAuthGuard]. It has nothing to do after the action: it returns [next.handle()] directly.

docs.title: 11.13.4. src/web/html-exception.filter.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/html-exception.filter.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A NestJS "exception filter" receives every exception that was not
// handled by the controllers' code. By default, NestJS answers in JSON
// ({"statusCode":403,"message":...}) - perfect for the JSON server, but
// unreadable in a browser. Instead, this filter builds a response
// suited to an HTML application:
//
//   401 (not logged in, or token expired) -> redirect to /login
//   403 (insufficient role)               -> error page "access forbidden"
//   404 (unknown page)                    -> error page "page not found"
//   400 (invalid parameter)               -> error page "invalid request"
//   everything else                       -> error page 500
//
// @Catch() without argument: the filter catches ALL exceptions. It is
// registered once for the whole application in main.ts.
// =========================================================================

import { ArgumentsHost, Catch, ExceptionFilter, HttpException, HttpStatus, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { COOKIE_JWT } from '../auth/auth.constants';
import { exposeUser, flash } from './view-context';

const MESSAGES: Record<number, string> = {
  [HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST]: 'ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST',
  [HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN]: 'ERRORS.FORBIDDEN',
  [HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND]: 'ERRORS.NOT_FOUND',
};

@Catch()
export class HtmlExceptionFilter implements ExceptionFilter {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(HtmlExceptionFilter.name);

  catch(exception: unknown, host: ArgumentsHost): void {
    const http = host.switchToHttp();
    const req = http.getRequest<Request>();
    const res = http.getResponse<Response>();

    const status = exception instanceof HttpException ? exception.getStatus() : HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;

    if (status === HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED) {
      // a cookie was present but is no longer valid: the session has expired
      if (req.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT]) {
        res.clearCookie(COOKIE_JWT, { path: '/' });
        flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED' });
      }
      res.redirect('/login');
      return;
    }

    if (status >= 500) {
      // a real anomaly: we keep the full trace in the server
      // console, without ever displaying it to the user
      this.logger.error(exception instanceof Error ? exception.stack : String(exception));
    }

    // the error page keeps the navigation bar of the logged-in user
    // (if any - a 403 occurs AFTER authentication)
    exposeUser(req, res);
    res.status(status).render('error', {
      pageTitle: 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE',
      code: status,
      message: MESSAGES[status] ?? 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR',
    });
  }
}
  • lines 25–29: the message key for each error code;
  • lines 42–50: a 401 redirects to the login page. If a token cookie was present, it has expired (or the account has been deleted): it is deleted, and the user is notified via a pop-up message;
  • lines 52–56: A genuine error is logged in the server console, along with its call stack, but is never disclosed to the user: these details would assist an attacker;
  • lines 60–65: the error page, with the logged-in user’s navigation bar.

docs.title: 11.13.5. src/web/application-model.service.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/application-model.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The cache / facade already present in the JSON server (equivalent of the
// [ApplicationModel] class of the Spring project): the lists of doctors and
// of clients are read once at startup, then served from memory.
//
// New: these lists can now CHANGE (the ADMIN adds,
// edits, deletes doctors and clients). A cache that would
// never be updated would display stale data: each write
// therefore goes through this service, which reloads the list concerned right after.
// That is the whole point of having a SINGLE entry point to the business
// layer: the rule "write => cache reload" is written only here.
// =========================================================================

import { Inject, Injectable, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PersonData, IBusiness, BUSINESS_TOKEN } from '../business/business.interface';
import { Client } from '../entities/client.entity';
import { Doctor } from '../entities/doctor.entity';
import { Slot } from '../entities/slot.entity';
import { Appointment } from '../entities/appointment.entity';
import { DoctorDaySchedule } from '../domain/doctor-day-schedule';

@Injectable()
export class ApplicationModelService implements IBusiness, OnModuleInit {
  private doctors: Doctor[] = [];
  private clients: Client[] = [];

  constructor(@Inject(BUSINESS_TOKEN) private readonly business: IBusiness) {}

  // if the database is unreachable at startup, the exception stops the server
  // with an explicit message - clearer, for an HTML application, than
  // starting "empty" and displaying empty lists.
  async onModuleInit(): Promise<void> {
    await this.reloadDoctors();
    await this.reloadClients();
  }

  private async reloadDoctors(): Promise<void> {
    this.doctors = await this.business.getAllDoctors();
  }

  private async reloadClients(): Promise<void> {
    this.clients = await this.business.getAllClients();
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

  async getAllDoctors(): Promise<Doctor[]> {
    return this.doctors;
  }

  async getAllClients(): Promise<Client[]> {
    return this.clients;
  }

  // the doctor whose user account is [userId] - used to preselect,
  // for a logged-in doctor, the doctor's own schedule
  getDoctorByUserId(userId: number): Doctor | null {
    return this.doctors.find((d) => d.userId === userId) ?? null;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

  getAllSlots(doctorId: number): Promise<Slot[]> {
    return this.business.getAllSlots(doctorId);
  }

  getDoctorDayAppointments(doctorId: number, day: string): Promise<Appointment[]> {
    return this.business.getDoctorDayAppointments(doctorId, day);
  }

  getClientById(id: number): Promise<Client | null> {
    return this.business.getClientById(id);
  }

  getDoctorById(id: number): Promise<Doctor | null> {
    return this.business.getDoctorById(id);
  }

  getAppointmentById(id: number): Promise<Appointment | null> {
    return this.business.getAppointmentById(id);
  }

  getSlotById(id: number): Promise<Slot | null> {
    return this.business.getSlotById(id);
  }

  getDoctorDaySchedule(doctorId: number, day: string): Promise<DoctorDaySchedule | null> {
    return this.business.getDoctorDaySchedule(doctorId, day);
  }

  // no cache here: the most recent data is what matters (a patient
  // who has just updated or deleted their account)
  getClientByUserId(userId: number): Promise<Client | null> {
    return this.business.getClientByUserId(userId);
  }

  getClientUpcomingAppointments(clientId: number): Promise<Appointment[]> {
    return this.business.getClientUpcomingAppointments(clientId);
  }

  addAppointment(day: string, slot: Slot, client: Client): Promise<Appointment> {
    return this.business.addAppointment(day, slot, client);
  }

  deleteAppointment(appointment: Appointment): Promise<void> {
    return this.business.deleteAppointment(appointment);
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------ writes => reload

  async addDoctor(data: PersonData): Promise<Doctor> {
    const doctor = await this.business.addDoctor(data);
    await this.reloadDoctors();
    return doctor;
  }

  async editDoctor(id: number, data: PersonData): Promise<Doctor> {
    const doctor = await this.business.editDoctor(id, data);
    await this.reloadDoctors();
    return doctor;
  }

  async deleteDoctor(id: number): Promise<void> {
    await this.business.deleteDoctor(id);
    await this.reloadDoctors();
  }

  async addClient(data: PersonData): Promise<Client> {
    const client = await this.business.addClient(data);
    await this.reloadClients();
    return client;
  }

  async editClient(id: number, data: PersonData): Promise<Client> {
    const client = await this.business.editClient(id, data);
    await this.reloadClients();
    return client;
  }

  async deleteClient(id: number): Promise<void> {
    await this.business.deleteClient(id);
    await this.reloadClients();
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 25: The service has the same interface as the business layer: for the controllers, it is the business layer. It sits between the two to store in memory (application scope, see Chapter 6) the lists of doctors and clients, which are displayed on almost every page;
  • line 29: the business layer is injected via its token;
  • lines 34–37: [onModuleInit] is called by [NestJS] once the module is built, before the server starts: the lists are read at startup. If the database is inaccessible, the application terminates with a clear message;
  • lines 49–55: The lists are served from memory;
  • lines 59–61: a doctor’s account: a logged-in doctor immediately sees their own schedule;
  • lines 65–109: other requests are forwarded as-is;
  • lines 113–145: any write operation involving doctors or clients refreshes the relevant list. Since this service is the sole entry point to the business layer, the rule “write = cache refresh” is implemented only here, and the cache cannot become stale.

docs.title: 11.13.6. src/web/views/handlebars-helpers.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/views/handlebars-helpers.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Handlebars is deliberately a LOGIC-LESS template language: no
// JavaScript expressions in the views, only {{variables}},
// {{#if}} / {{#each}} blocks... When a view needs a little more, we
// give it a "helper": a TypeScript function, callable from the view.
//
// The application needs only four helpers:
//   {{t 'KEY'}}                      translation (the equivalent of the `| translate` pipe)
//   {{t 'KEY' name=person.lastName}} translation with parameter(s)
//   {{#if (eq a b)}}                 equality comparison
//   {{#if (or a b)}}                 true if at least one of the arguments is true
//   {{active currentPath '/doctors'}} "active" if the current page is under this path
// =========================================================================

import { HelperOptions } from 'handlebars';
import { Language, DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, isLanguage, translate } from '../i18n';

// the 'hbs' module has no type declarations: we describe here the little
// we use of it
interface Hbs {
  registerHelper(name: string, fn: (...args: any[]) => unknown): void;
}

export function registerHelpers(hbs: Hbs): void {
  // The last argument received by a helper is always the Handlebars [options]
  // object: options.hash contains the named parameters (name=...), and
  // options.data.root the FULL model of the page - hence also res.locals.lang,
  // the chosen language (see view-context.ts), even inside an {{#each}}.
  hbs.registerHelper('t', (key: unknown, options: HelperOptions) => {
    const lang = options.data?.root?.lang;
    const language: Language = isLanguage(lang) ? lang : DEFAULT_LANGUAGE;
    // the returned text is then escaped by Handlebars ({{ }} and not {{{ }}}):
    // a name entered by the user therefore cannot inject HTML
    return typeof key === 'string' ? translate(language, key, options.hash) : '';
  });

  hbs.registerHelper('eq', (a: unknown, b: unknown) => a === b);

  // ...args: all the arguments; the last one is the Handlebars [options]
  // object (see above), which we set aside before testing the others
  hbs.registerHelper('or', (...args: unknown[]) => args.slice(0, -1).some(Boolean));

  hbs.registerHelper('active', (path: unknown, prefix: unknown) =>
    typeof path === 'string' && typeof prefix === 'string' && path.startsWith(prefix) ? 'active' : '',
  );
}
  • lines 31–37: the translation helper (see Example 22);
  • line 39: the equality check (see Example 16);
  • line 43: true if any of the arguments is true. [...args] receives all the arguments; the last one is the [options] object from [Handlebars], which is discarded;
  • lines 45–47: the [active] class of the current menu (see Example 16).

docs.title: 11.13.7. src/web/models/person-form.dto.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/models/person-form.dto.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The fields of the "person" forms and their constraints. Three
// forms share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name):
//
//   PersonFieldsDto                 title, firstName, lastName
//    ├─ PersonFormDto               + OPTIONAL login / password, version
//    │                                (the ADMIN adds or edits a doctor / client)
//    ├─ RegistrationFormDto         + REQUIRED login / password / confirmation
//    │                                (a patient creates their account)
//    └─ MyAccountFormDto            + login, optional new password,
//                                     CURRENT password required, version
//                                     (a patient edits their account)
//
// Class inheritance also applies to class-validator decorators:
// a child class inherits the constraints of the fields of its parent class.
//
// The error messages are translation KEYS (see i18n/*.json).
// @Transform(...) (class-transformer) cleans the input BEFORE the
// validation: extra spaces removed, optional fields left empty
// turned into `undefined`, login put in lower case, version converted to a number
// (everything that comes from an HTML form is a character string).
//
// The "password = confirmation" check involves TWO fields: it
// is done by the controller, after the validation of each field.
// =========================================================================

import { Transform } from 'class-transformer';
import { IsIn, IsInt, IsNotEmpty, IsOptional, Matches, MaxLength, MinLength } from 'class-validator';

export const TITLES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

const clean = ({ value }: { value: unknown }) => (typeof value === 'string' ? value.trim() : value);
const emptyToUndefined = ({ value }: { value: unknown }) =>
  typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() !== '' ? value.trim() : undefined;
const cleanLogin = ({ value }: { value: unknown }) => emptyToUndefined({ value })?.toLowerCase();
// a password is not "cleaned" (spaces may be part of it)
const passwordOrUndefined = ({ value }: { value: unknown }) =>
  typeof value === 'string' && value !== '' ? value : undefined;
const numberOrUndefined = ({ value }: { value: unknown }) =>
  value === undefined || value === '' ? undefined : Number(value);

// login: lower-case letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore - 30 characters at most
const LOGIN_FORMAT = /^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/;
// minimum length of a password CHOSEN by a patient
export const PASSWORD_MIN = 6;

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ common base
export class PersonFieldsDto {
  @IsIn(TITLES, { message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE' })
  title: string;

  // maximum lengths = those of the SQL columns (VARCHAR(20))
  @Transform(clean)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED' })
  @MaxLength(20, { message: 'ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG' })
  firstName: string;

  @Transform(clean)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED' })
  @MaxLength(20, { message: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG' })
  lastName: string;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ ADMIN
export class PersonFormDto extends PersonFieldsDto {
  // optional (see PersonData, business.interface.ts)
  @Transform(cleanLogin)
  @IsOptional()
  @Matches(LOGIN_FORMAT, { message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN' })
  login?: string;

  // optional; 72 characters at most (beyond that, bcrypt ignores the rest)
  @Transform(passwordOrUndefined)
  @IsOptional()
  @MaxLength(72, { message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG' })
  password?: string;

  // hidden field of the edit form (optimistic lock)
  @Transform(numberOrUndefined)
  @IsOptional()
  @IsInt({ message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM' })
  version?: number;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ registration of a patient
export class RegistrationFormDto extends PersonFieldsDto {
  @Transform(cleanLogin)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED' })
  @Matches(LOGIN_FORMAT, { message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN' })
  login: string;

  @Transform(passwordOrUndefined)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED' })
  @MinLength(PASSWORD_MIN, { message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT' })
  @MaxLength(72, { message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG' })
  password: string;

  @Transform(passwordOrUndefined)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED' })
  confirmation: string;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Manage my account"
export class MyAccountFormDto extends PersonFieldsDto {
  @Transform(cleanLogin)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED' })
  @Matches(LOGIN_FORMAT, { message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN' })
  login: string;

  // optional: empty = password unchanged
  @Transform(passwordOrUndefined)
  @IsOptional()
  @MinLength(PASSWORD_MIN, { message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT' })
  @MaxLength(72, { message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG' })
  password?: string;

  @Transform(passwordOrUndefined)
  @IsOptional()
  confirmation?: string;

  // the CURRENT password, required for any change to the account
  @Transform(passwordOrUndefined)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED' })
  currentPassword: string;

  @Transform(numberOrUndefined)
  @IsOptional()
  @IsInt({ message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM' })
  version?: number;
}

// =========================================================================
// web/helpers/form.helper.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Validation of an HTML form with class-validator.
//
// The JSON server left validation to the global ValidationPipe: on
// error, it answered 400 Bad Request itself - which suits a
// JavaScript client, which then displays the error its own way. For an HTML
// page, on the contrary, we want to DISPLAY the form AGAIN, with the values
// already entered and a message under each invalid field. So we call
// class-validator ourselves, to keep control over what happens next.
// =========================================================================

import { ClassConstructor, plainToInstance } from 'class-transformer';
import { validate } from 'class-validator';
import { TITLES } from '../models/person-form.dto';

// errors by field: { lastName: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED', ... } - each
// message is a translation KEY (see the decorators of the DTOs)
export type FormErrors = Record<string, string>;

export interface ValidationResult<T> {
  dto: T; // the data, converted and cleaned (see the @Transform of the DTOs)
  errors: FormErrors | null; // null = valid form
}

export async function validateForm<T extends object>(
  cls: ClassConstructor<T>,
  body: Record<string, unknown>,
): Promise<ValidationResult<T>> {
  // plainToInstance: turns the plain object received ({ lastName: ' dupont ' })
  // into an instance of the DTO class, applying its @Transform(...)
  const dto = plainToInstance(cls, body);
  // validate: checks all the constraints (@IsNotEmpty, @MaxLength...);
  // forbidUnknownValues:false because we validate an object we built
  const violations = await validate(dto, { forbidUnknownValues: false });
  if (violations.length === 0) {
    return { dto, errors: null };
  }
  const errors: FormErrors = {};
  for (const violation of violations) {
    // we keep only the first message of each field
    errors[violation.property] = Object.values(violation.constraints ?? {})[0] ?? 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM';
  }
  return { dto, errors };
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the form fields concerned by each "input" business error
// (a duplicate): they are framed in red, the message being at the bottom of the page
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export const BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS: Record<string, string[]> = {
  'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN': ['login'],
  'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS': ['firstName', 'lastName'],
  'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS': ['firstName', 'lastName'],
};

// { firstName: true, lastName: true }: the fields to frame in red (is-invalid) -
// those that have a validation message, plus possible others
export function invalidFields(errors: FormErrors, others: string[] = []): Record<string, boolean> {
  const fields: Record<string, boolean> = {};
  for (const field of [...Object.keys(errors), ...others]) {
    fields[field] = true;
  }
  return fields;
}

// the options of the "Title" drop-down list, the one of [value] selected
export function titleOptions(value: string): { value: string; selected: boolean }[] {
  return TITLES.map((t) => ({ value: t, selected: t === value }));
}
  • lines 27–30: Form validation, as in Example 19. The option [forbidUnknownValues: false] is required because we are validating an object generated by [plainToInstance], not one received from [ValidationPipe];
  • lines 52–56: certain business errors relate to specific fields (e.g., a username that is already taken): these fields will be highlighted in red, with the message appearing at the bottom of the page;
  • lines 60–66: the fields to be highlighted in red;
  • lines 69–71: the options in the list of titles, with the selected one highlighted (see example 18).

// =========================================================================
// web/helpers/dates.helper.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Small functions on dates in the "yyyy-MM-dd" format (that of the
// appointments.day column and of the <input type="date"> field of the forms).
// =========================================================================

// today's date: defined in the business layer, which needs it for
// its business rules - we simply re-export it here
export { today } from '../../business/dates';

// true if [day] is a date that exists, in the yyyy-MM-dd format
// (same check as the JSON server: "2026-02-30" is refused)
export function isValidDate(day: unknown): day is string {
  if (typeof day !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(day)) {
    return false;
  }
  const date = new Date(`${day}T00:00:00Z`);
  return !isNaN(date.getTime()) && date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) === day;
}

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
export function formatTime(h: number, m: number): string {
  return `${h}:${twoDigits(m)}`;
}

// "mercredi 23 septembre 2026" / "Wednesday 23 September 2026", depending on the language
// (Intl.DateTimeFormat: the date formatting API built into JavaScript)
export function formatDay(day: string, language: string): string {
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(language === 'en' ? 'en-GB' : 'fr-FR', {
    dateStyle: 'full',
    timeZone: 'UTC', // "2026-09-23T00:00:00Z" must remain the 23rd, whatever the server's time zone
  }).format(new Date(`${day}T00:00:00Z`));
}

function twoDigits(n: number): string {
  return n.toString().padStart(2, '0');
}
  • Line 10: The current date is defined in the business layer; this module re-exports it: controllers import all date functions from a single location;
  • lines 14–20: a [yyyy-mm-dd] date that exists (see Example 12);
  • lines 29–34: a date spelled out in full, depending on the language. The [timeZone: 'UTC'] option prevents a one-day offset when the server is not set to Greenwich Mean Time.

// =========================================================================
// web/helpers/patient.helper.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The patient (Client entity) matching the logged-in user.
//
// The JWT token contains only the id of the ACCOUNT (users.id). For a USER role,
// the matching client is found through the clients.user column.
//
// If there is none, the account has been deleted since login
// (by the patient themselves in another tab, or by the ADMIN) while
// the token is still valid: we treat it as an expired session
// (UnauthorizedException -> back to the login page, see
// HtmlExceptionFilter).
// =========================================================================

import { UnauthorizedException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ApplicationModelService } from '../application-model.service';
import { ConnectedUser } from '../../auth/jwt.strategy';
import { Client } from '../../entities/client.entity';
import { Person } from '../../entities/person.entity';

// "Mme Alice DURAND"
export function label(p: Person): string {
  return `${p.title} ${p.firstName} ${p.lastName}`;
}

export async function connectedPatient(
  application: ApplicationModelService,
  user: ConnectedUser,
): Promise<Client> {
  const client = await application.getClientByUserId(user.userId);
  if (client === null) {
    throw new UnauthorizedException();
  }
  return client;
}

// =========================================================================
// web/controllers/language.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two FR / EN buttons of the
// navigation bar. The choice is stored in a cookie (the Angular client
// kept it in localStorage), then we go back to the page we came from.
// Unprotected route: the language must be changeable before logging in.
// =========================================================================

import { Controller, Get, NotFoundException, Param, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { isLanguage } from '../i18n';
import { COOKIE_LANGUAGE } from '../view-context';

const ONE_YEAR = 365 * 24 * 3600 * 1000;

@Controller('language')
export class LanguageController {
  @Get(':language')
  change(@Param('language') language: string, @Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response): void {
    if (!isLanguage(language)) {
      throw new NotFoundException();
    }
    res.cookie(COOKIE_LANGUAGE, language, { maxAge: ONE_YEAR, sameSite: 'lax', httpOnly: true });
    res.redirect(originPage(req));
  }
}

// the previous page, according to the HTTP "Referer" header sent by the
// browser. Only its path is kept (/schedule?...): redirecting to
// a full address supplied by the request would allow sending
// the user to another site (so-called "open redirect" flaw).
function originPage(req: Request): string {
  const referer = req.get('referer');
  if (!referer) {
    return '/';
  }
  try {
    const url = new URL(referer);
    return url.pathname.startsWith('/language/') ? '/' : url.pathname + url.search;
  } catch {
    return '/';
  }
}

The controller from Example 22. Note: if the original page is itself a [/language/...] page (line 40), the request is redirected to the site’s root to prevent an infinite loop.

docs.title: 11.14.2. src/web/controllers/schedule.controller.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/controllers/schedule.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The schedule page: choice of a doctor and a day, schedule of that
// doctor on that day, booking and cancelling appointments.
// It is the server-side equivalent of the Angular components
// <app-doctor-day-picker>, <app-agenda> and <app-booking-dialog>.
//
//   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23                the page
//   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7         the same page, with
//                                                           the booking dialog
//                                                           of slot 7 open
//   POST /schedule/book                                     creates an appointment
//   POST /schedule/cancel                                   cancels an appointment
//
// The whole page is described by its URL: you can reload it, bookmark it,
// use the browser's "Back" button - without a single line
// of JavaScript.
//
// What each user sees and can do:
//
//   | role          | occupied slot displayed           | Book               | Cancel  |
//   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
//   | ADMIN, DOCTOR | name of the patient               | for a patient      | yes     |
//   |               |                                   | chosen in a list   |         |
//   | USER (patient)| "Booked", or THEIR name if it is  | for themselves, if | no (*)  |
//   |               | their own appointment             | they have no       |         |
//   |               |                                   | upcoming one       |         |
//
//   (*) the patient cancels their appointment from their "My area" page.
//
// CONFIDENTIALITY: for a patient, the name of the OTHER patients is not
// simply hidden by the view - it is never put in the model
// passed to the view. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it,
// not even hidden (a simple "View page source" would reveal it otherwise).
//
// No booking in the past: the "Book" button only appears
// for today and the following days (and the business layer would refuse it
// anyway).
// =========================================================================

import { BadRequestException, Body, Controller, Get, Post, Query, Render, Req, Res, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { ApplicationModelService } from '../application-model.service';
import { JwtAuthGuard } from '../../auth/jwt-auth.guard';
import { RolesGuard } from '../../auth/roles.guard';
import { Roles } from '../../auth/roles.decorator';
import { ConnectedUser } from '../../auth/jwt.strategy';
import { BusinessException } from '../../business/business.exception';
import { flash } from '../view-context';
import { today, isValidDate, formatTime } from '../helpers/dates.helper';
import { label, connectedPatient } from '../helpers/patient.helper';
import { Client } from '../../entities/client.entity';
import { Person } from '../../entities/person.entity';

type AuthenticatedRequest = Request & { user: ConnectedUser };

// ----------------------------------------------------------------- view model
// (what views/schedule.hbs displays - only data already formatted
// AND already filtered according to the role: the view decides nothing)

interface OptionView {
  id: number;
  label: string; // "Mme Marie PELISSIER"
  selected: boolean;
}

interface ScheduleRowView {
  slotId: number;
  time: string; // "8:00 - 8:20"
  free: boolean;
  patient: string | null; // name displayed for an occupied slot; null = "Booked"
  mine: boolean; // the appointment of the logged-in patient
  bookable: boolean; // display the "Book" button?
  bookUrl: string;
  appointmentId: number | null; // set only if the "Cancel" button is displayed
}

interface ScheduleView {
  doctor: string;
  day: string;
  rows: ScheduleRowView[];
}

interface BookingView {
  slotId: number;
  time: string;
  // ADMIN / DOCTOR: the list of patients to choose from
  clients: OptionView[];
  // USER: the patient is the user themselves
  patient: string | null;
}

export interface ScheduleModel {
  pageTitle: string;
  doctors: OptionView[];
  doctorId: number | null;
  day: string;
  schedule: ScheduleView | null;
  booking: BookingView | null;
  backUrl: string; // the displayed schedule, without the booking dialog
  // patient who already has an upcoming appointment: the message that explains
  // why there is no "Book" button
  info: string | null;
  error: string | null;
}

// what the controller knows about the user, to decide what to display
interface Rights {
  manager: boolean; // ADMIN or DOCTOR
  patient: Client | null; // the logged-in client (USER role), null otherwise
  patientCanBook: boolean; // USER without an upcoming appointment
}

@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard)
@Controller('schedule')
export class ScheduleController {
  constructor(private readonly application: ApplicationModelService) {}

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /schedule
  // @Render('schedule'): the object returned by the method becomes the model of
  // the view views/schedule.hbs (+ the content of res.locals, see view-context.ts).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Get()
  @Render('schedule')
  async show(
    @Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest,
    @Query('doctorId') rawDoctorId?: string,
    @Query('day') rawDay?: string,
    @Query('book') rawBook?: string,
  ): Promise<ScheduleModel> {
    let error: string | null = null;
    const rights = await this.rights(req.user);

    // the day: the one in the URL if it is valid, today otherwise
    let day = today();
    if (rawDay !== undefined) {
      if (isValidDate(rawDay)) {
        day = rawDay;
      } else {
        error = 'ERRORS.INVALID_DATE';
      }
    }
    const dayBookable = day >= today();

    // the doctor: the one in the URL; failing that, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves
    let doctorId = positiveInteger(rawDoctorId);
    if (rawDoctorId === undefined && req.user.role === 'DOCTOR') {
      doctorId = this.application.getDoctorByUserId(req.user.userId)?.id ?? null;
    }

    const doctors = (await this.application.getAllDoctors()).map((d) => option(d, d.id === doctorId));

    // the schedule, if a doctor is chosen (and the date is valid)
    let schedule: ScheduleView | null = null;
    if (doctorId !== null && error === null) {
      const doctorSchedule = await this.application.getDoctorDaySchedule(doctorId, day);
      if (doctorSchedule === null) {
        error = 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND';
      } else {
        schedule = {
          doctor: label(doctorSchedule.doctor),
          day,
          rows: doctorSchedule.doctorDaySlots.map(({ slot, appointment }) => {
            const free = appointment === null;
            // the appointment of the logged-in patient?
            const mine = !free && rights.patient !== null && appointment.clientId === rights.patient.id;
            return {
              slotId: slot.id,
              time: `${formatTime(slot.startHour, slot.startMinute)} - ${formatTime(slot.endHour, slot.endMinute)}`,
              free,
              // THE confidentiality point: a patient receives the name only
              // of THEIR appointment; for the others, null (the view displays "Booked")
              patient: free ? null : rights.manager || mine ? label(appointment.client) : null,
              mine,
              bookable: free && dayBookable && (rights.manager || rights.patientCanBook),
              bookUrl: scheduleUrl(doctorId as number, day, slot.id),
              appointmentId: !free && rights.manager ? appointment.id : null,
            };
          }),
        };
      }
    }

    // the booking dialog: only if the requested slot is
    // bookable by this user
    let booking: BookingView | null = null;
    const slotId = positiveInteger(rawBook);
    const row = schedule?.rows.find((r) => r.slotId === slotId && r.bookable);
    if (row) {
      booking = {
        slotId: row.slotId,
        time: row.time,
        clients: rights.manager ? (await this.application.getAllClients()).map((c) => option(c, false)) : [],
        patient: rights.patient ? label(rights.patient) : null,
      };
    }

    return {
      pageTitle: 'SCHEDULE.PAGE_TITLE',
      doctors,
      doctorId,
      day,
      schedule,
      booking,
      backUrl: doctorId !== null ? scheduleUrl(doctorId, day) : '/schedule',
      info: rights.patient !== null && !rights.patientCanBook ? 'SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO' : null,
      error,
    };
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /schedule/book   fields: doctorId, day, slotId, clientId
  //
  // For a patient (USER), the clientId field is IGNORED: they always book
  // for themselves. Trusting a field sent by the
  // browser would let a clever patient book in someone else's name.
  //
  // "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern: whatever the result, we do not
  // build a page here - we set a flash message and redirect
  // to the schedule (see flash(), view-context.ts).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post('book')
  @Roles('ADMIN', 'DOCTOR', 'USER')
  async book(
    @Body() body: Record<string, string>,
    @Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const { doctorId, day } = readScheduleRequest(body);
    const slotId = positiveInteger(body.slotId);
    if (slotId === null) {
      throw new BadRequestException();
    }

    let client: Client | null;
    if (req.user.role === 'USER') {
      client = await connectedPatient(this.application, req.user);
    } else {
      const clientId = positiveInteger(body.clientId);
      if (clientId === null) {
        // no patient chosen: the booking dialog is opened again
        flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT' });
        return res.redirect(scheduleUrl(doctorId, day, slotId));
      }
      client = await this.application.getClientById(clientId);
    }

    const slot = await this.application.getSlotById(slotId);
    if (client === null) {
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND' });
    } else if (slot === null || slot.doctorId !== doctorId) {
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND' });
    } else {
      try {
        // the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
        // patient, free slot) are checked by the business layer
        await this.application.addAppointment(day, slot, client);
        flash(res, { type: 'success', key: 'SCHEDULE.BOOKED' });
      } catch (e) {
        // same rule, but a message in the 2nd person when it is the patient
        // themselves who books ("You already have..." rather than "This patient...")
        if (
          req.user.role === 'USER' &&
          e instanceof BusinessException &&
          e.key === 'ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT'
        ) {
          flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO' });
        } else {
          flashBusinessError(res, e);
        }
      }
    }
    res.redirect(scheduleUrl(doctorId, day));
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /schedule/cancel   fields: appointmentId, doctorId, day
  // (a patient cancels THEIR appointment from "My area", not from here)
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post('cancel')
  @Roles('ADMIN', 'DOCTOR')
  async cancel(@Body() body: Record<string, string>, @Res() res: Response): Promise<void> {
    const { doctorId, day } = readScheduleRequest(body);
    const appointmentId = positiveInteger(body.appointmentId);
    if (appointmentId === null) {
      throw new BadRequestException();
    }
    const appointment = await this.application.getAppointmentById(appointmentId);
    if (appointment === null) {
      // already cancelled (by someone else, or double click)
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND' });
    } else {
      await this.application.deleteAppointment(appointment);
      flash(res, { type: 'success', key: 'SCHEDULE.CANCELLED' });
    }
    res.redirect(scheduleUrl(doctorId, day));
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // who is logged in, and what are they allowed to do on this page?
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private async rights(user: ConnectedUser): Promise<Rights> {
    if (user.role !== 'USER') {
      return { manager: true, patient: null, patientCanBook: false };
    }
    const patient = await connectedPatient(this.application, user);
    const upcoming = await this.application.getClientUpcomingAppointments(patient.id);
    return { manager: false, patient, patientCanBook: upcoming.length === 0 };
  }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------- utility functions

// "3" -> 3 ; "", "abc", "-2", undefined -> null
function positiveInteger(value: unknown): number | null {
  const n = Number(value);
  return typeof value === 'string' && value !== '' && Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 ? n : null;
}

// the hidden doctorId / day fields, common to both POST forms
function readScheduleRequest(body: Record<string, string>): { doctorId: number; day: string } {
  const doctorId = positiveInteger(body.doctorId);
  if (doctorId === null || !isValidDate(body.day)) {
    throw new BadRequestException(); // -> "invalid request" page (see HtmlExceptionFilter)
  }
  return { doctorId, day: body.day };
}

function scheduleUrl(doctorId: number, day: string, book?: number): string {
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ doctorId: String(doctorId), day });
  if (book !== undefined) {
    params.set('book', String(book));
  }
  return `/schedule?${params.toString()}`;
}

function option(p: Person, selected: boolean): OptionView {
  return { id: p.id, label: label(p), selected };
}

// a BusinessException becomes a flash message; any other error is a
// real anomaly, which we let bubble up to HtmlExceptionFilter
function flashBusinessError(res: Response, e: unknown): void {
  if (e instanceof BusinessException) {
    flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: e.key, params: e.params });
    return;
  }
  throw e;
}

The application’s main page. Let’s walk through this code section by section.

docs.title: 11.14.2.1. The URL section of the page
docs.text: The comments on lines 9–14 describe the routes. Note that the booking window is not opened by [JavaScript]: it is a parameter of URL ([book=7]) that instructs the server to display the page with the window open. The “Book” button is therefore simply a link. The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, bookmark it, or use the browser’s “Back” button.

docs.title: 11.14.2.2. The view template
docs.text:
• line 56: the type of request for a protected route: an [Express] request whose [user] field was set by [JwtAuthGuard];
  • lines 62–106: The view template is typed. The view receives only data that has already been formatted ([time: "8:00 - 8:20"]) and filtered according to the user’s role; it does not make any decisions. In [ScheduleRowView] (lines 68–77), [patient] is equal to [null] when the user does not have permission to view the patient’s name; [bookable] and [appointmentId] determine whether the “Book” and “Cancel” buttons should be displayed;
  • lines 109–113: what the controller knows about the logged-in user.

docs.title: 11.14.2.3. GET /schedule
docs.text:
• lines 115–116: All routes require a logged-in user. Without [@Roles] on the class, all roles have access to the page;
  • lines 127–132: the three parameters of URL, all optional, received as strings and converted later;
  • lines 137–145: the requested date, if valid; otherwise, today. Appointments can only be booked starting today;
  • lines 148–151: the requested doctor; otherwise, a logged-in doctor sees their own schedule;
  • line 153: the drop-down list of doctors, retrieved from the cache;
  • lines 157–184: the calendar, calculated by the business layer, is converted into table rows. Line 175 is the application’s privacy checkpoint: a patient receives only the name of their own appointment. For others, the model contains [null], and the view displays “Booked.” The name is not simply hidden by the view: it is never sent to the browser;
  • lines 188–198: the booking window opens only if the requested time slot is bookable by that user. An administrator selects the patient from a list; a patient books for themselves;

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/controllers/persons.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The management of doctors and that of clients (reserved for the ADMIN) are
// IDENTICAL: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
// writing the same routes twice, we write them once in this
// ABSTRACT class, inherited by DoctorsController (@Controller('doctors'))
// and ClientsController (@Controller('clients')). Each subclass only
// has to provide its "configuration": which methods to call, which
// labels to display.
//
// The route decorators (@Get, @Post...) set HERE are inherited: NestJS
// walks the whole prototype chain of the controller class. We
// therefore get, for each of the two subclasses:
//
//   GET  /doctors                    list
//   GET  /doctors/add                empty form
//   POST /doctors/add                creation
//   GET  /doctors/:id/edit           pre-filled form
//   POST /doctors/:id/edit           update
//   POST /doctors/:id/delete         deletion
//
// (and the same URLs under /clients). The views are shared too:
// views/persons/list.hbs and views/persons/form.hbs.
// =========================================================================

import { Body, Get, HttpCode, NotFoundException, Param, ParseIntPipe, Post, Render, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Response } from 'express';
import { ApplicationModelService } from '../application-model.service';
import { PersonData } from '../../business/business.interface';
import { BusinessException } from '../../business/business.exception';
import { Person } from '../../entities/person.entity';
import { flash } from '../view-context';
import {
  BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS,
  FormErrors,
  invalidFields,
  titleOptions,
  validateForm,
} from '../helpers/form.helper';
import { PersonFormDto } from '../models/person-form.dto';

// the translation keys specific to each type of person
export interface PersonKeys {
  title: string; // "Doctors"
  add: string; // "Add a doctor"
  edit: string; // "Edit a doctor"
  empty: string; // "No doctors."
  confirmDelete: string; // "Delete this doctor and their account?"
  added: string; // "Doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
  edited: string;
  deleted: string;
}

export interface PersonsConfig<T extends Person> {
  url: string; // '/doctors' or '/clients'
  keys: PersonKeys;
  list(): Promise<T[]>;
  find(id: number): Promise<T | null>;
  add(data: PersonData): Promise<T>;
  edit(id: number, data: PersonData): Promise<T>;
  delete(id: number): Promise<void>;
}

// the values displayed in the fields of the form
interface FormValues {
  title: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  login: string;
  version: number | null;
}

export abstract class PersonsController<T extends Person> {
  protected abstract readonly config: PersonsConfig<T>;

  constructor(protected readonly application: ApplicationModelService) {}

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /doctors (or /clients)
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Get()
  @Render('persons/list')
  async list() {
    const persons = await this.config.list();
    return {
      pageTitle: this.config.keys.title,
      keys: this.config.keys,
      addUrl: `${this.config.url}/add`,
      persons: persons.map((p) => ({
        title: p.title,
        firstName: p.firstName,
        lastName: p.lastName,
        login: p.user?.login ?? '',
        editUrl: `${this.config.url}/${p.id}/edit`,
        deleteUrl: `${this.config.url}/${p.id}/delete`,
      })),
    };
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /doctors/add
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Get('add')
  addForm(@Res() res: Response): void {
    this.showForm(res, null, { title: 'Mr', firstName: '', lastName: '', login: '', version: null });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /doctors/add
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post('add')
  @HttpCode(200) // if the form is displayed again (see auth.controller.ts)
  async add(@Body() body: Record<string, unknown>, @Res() res: Response): Promise<void> {
    const { dto, errors } = await validateForm(PersonFormDto, body);
    if (errors !== null) {
      return this.showForm(res, null, enteredValues(dto), errors);
    }
    try {
      const person = await this.config.add(dto);
      flash(res, { type: 'success', key: this.config.keys.added, params: messageParams(person) });
      res.redirect(this.config.url);
    } catch (e) {
      this.showBusinessError(res, null, enteredValues(dto), e);
    }
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /doctors/:id/edit
  // ParseIntPipe: if :id is not an integer, NestJS throws a
  // BadRequestException ("invalid request" page, see HtmlExceptionFilter)
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Get(':id/edit')
  async editForm(@Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number, @Res() res: Response): Promise<void> {
    const person = await this.config.find(id);
    if (person === null) {
      throw new NotFoundException();
    }
    this.showForm(res, id, {
      title: person.title,
      firstName: person.firstName,
      lastName: person.lastName,
      login: person.user?.login ?? '',
      version: person.version,
    });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /doctors/:id/edit
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post(':id/edit')
  @HttpCode(200)
  async edit(
    @Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number,
    @Body() body: Record<string, unknown>,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const { dto, errors } = await validateForm(PersonFormDto, body);
    if (errors !== null) {
      return this.showForm(res, id, enteredValues(dto), errors);
    }
    try {
      const person = await this.config.edit(id, dto);
      flash(res, { type: 'success', key: this.config.keys.edited, params: messageParams(person) });
      res.redirect(this.config.url);
    } catch (e) {
      this.showBusinessError(res, id, enteredValues(dto), e);
    }
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /doctors/:id/delete
  // (the "Are you sure?" confirmation is requested by the browser before
  // the form is sent, see public/js/app.js)
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post(':id/delete')
  async delete(@Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number, @Res() res: Response): Promise<void> {
    const person = await this.config.find(id);
    try {
      await this.config.delete(id);
      flash(res, { type: 'success', key: this.config.keys.deleted, params: messageParams(person) });
    } catch (e) {
      if (!(e instanceof BusinessException)) {
        throw e;
      }
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: e.key, params: e.params });
    }
    res.redirect(this.config.url);
  }

  // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

  // id === null: creation form; otherwise: edit form
  //   errors          : message under each field refused by validation
  //   error           : THE error message of the page, displayed at the bottom of the page
  //                     (see views/partials/errors.hbs)
  //   otherFields     : fields to frame in red WITHOUT their own message (e.g.:
  //                     first + last name of a namesake - the message is at the bottom)
  private showForm(
    res: Response,
    id: number | null,
    values: FormValues,
    errors: FormErrors = {},
    error: string | null = null,
    otherFields: string[] = [],
  ): void {
    const creating = id === null;
    res.render('persons/form', {
      pageTitle: creating ? this.config.keys.add : this.config.keys.edit,
      creating,
      action: creating ? `${this.config.url}/add` : `${this.config.url}/${id}/edit`,
      listUrl: this.config.url,
      values,
      titles: titleOptions(values.title),
      errors,
      invalidFields: invalidFields(errors, otherFields),
      error: error ?? (Object.keys(errors).length > 0 ? 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM' : null),
    });
  }

  // a business rule refused the write: the form is displayed again,
  // with the user's input and the message of the business layer
  private showBusinessError(res: Response, id: number | null, values: FormValues, e: unknown): void {
    if (!(e instanceof BusinessException)) {
      throw e; // real anomaly -> HtmlExceptionFilter (page 500)
    }
    if (e.key === 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND' || e.key === 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND') {
      // deleted in the meantime by another ADMIN: back to the list
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: e.key });
      return res.redirect(this.config.url);
    }
    // the message goes at the bottom of the page; the fields concerned, if any, are
    // framed in red so that the user immediately sees what to correct
    this.showForm(res, id, values, {}, e.key, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS[e.key] ?? []);
  }
}

// what the user entered (password excluded: it is never sent back to the browser)
function enteredValues(dto: PersonFormDto): FormValues {
  return {
    title: dto.title ?? '',
    firstName: typeof dto.firstName === 'string' ? dto.firstName : '',
    lastName: typeof dto.lastName === 'string' ? dto.lastName : '',
    login: dto.login ?? '',
    version: dto.version ?? null,
  };
}

// {name} and {login} of the "added / updated / deleted" messages
function messageParams(person: Person | null): Record<string, string> {
  if (person === null) {
    return { name: '', login: '' };
  }
  return { name: `${person.firstName} ${person.lastName}`, login: person.user?.login ?? '' };
}

The handling of doctors and clients is identical. Rather than writing two similar controllers, we create an abstract class from which both controllers inherit.

  • lines 44–53: the texts specific to each type of person (translation keys);
  • lines 55–63: the configuration provided by each subclass: the base URL, the texts, and the functions to call for listing, searching, adding, modifying, and deleting;
  • line 75: an abstract field: each subclass must define it;
  • lines 82–99: the list. Route decorators applied to a parent class are inherited: [NestJS] finds them by traversing the prototype chain. The model contains, for each person, the URL for their buttons;
  • lines 104–107 and 112–126: the addition, in three steps, as in Example 28: validation, business layer, PRG;
  • lines 133–146 and 151–157: modification. [ParseIntPipe] rejects a non-numeric identifier (error 400);
  • lines 176–189: deletion. The person is retrieved beforehand to display their name in the confirmation message;
  • lines 199–206: the form, for both creation ([id === null]) and modification;
  • lines 223–235: a person who has been deleted in the meantime is returned to the list; other business errors redisplay the form, with the relevant fields highlighted in red;
  • lines 239–247: the values to be redisplayed (never the password).

// =========================================================================
// web/controllers/doctors.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Management of the doctors (ADMIN role only). All the routes are
// inherited from PersonsController (see persons.controller.ts): all that
// remains here is to say WHAT to call and WHICH labels to display.
//
// @Roles('ADMIN') set on the CLASS applies to all its routes,
// including the inherited ones (RolesGuard looks for the metadata on the method,
// then on the class - see auth/roles.guard.ts).
// =========================================================================

import { Controller, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
import { JwtAuthGuard } from '../../auth/jwt-auth.guard';
import { RolesGuard } from '../../auth/roles.guard';
import { Roles } from '../../auth/roles.decorator';
import { ApplicationModelService } from '../application-model.service';
import { Doctor } from '../../entities/doctor.entity';
import { PersonsConfig, PersonsController } from './persons.controller';

@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard)
@Roles('ADMIN')
@Controller('doctors')
export class DoctorsController extends PersonsController<Doctor> {
  protected readonly config: PersonsConfig<Doctor> = {
    url: '/doctors',
    keys: {
      title: 'DOCTORS.TITLE',
      add: 'DOCTORS.ADD',
      edit: 'DOCTORS.EDIT',
      empty: 'DOCTORS.EMPTY',
      confirmDelete: 'DOCTORS.DELETE_CONFIRM',
      added: 'DOCTORS.ADDED',
      edited: 'DOCTORS.UPDATED',
      deleted: 'DOCTORS.DELETED',
    },
    list: () => this.application.getAllDoctors(),
    find: (id) => this.application.getDoctorById(id),
    add: (data) => this.application.addDoctor(data),
    edit: (id, data) => this.application.editDoctor(id, data),
    delete: (id) => this.application.deleteDoctor(id),
  };

  // an explicit constructor, so that TypeScript emits on THIS class
  // the type metadata of the parameters, which NestJS needs to
  // know what to inject (the parent class, abstract and without a decorator,
  // has none)
  constructor(application: ApplicationModelService) {
    super(application);
  }
}

// =========================================================================
// web/controllers/registration.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "Create a patient account": a patient who does not have an account yet
// creates it themselves. UNPROTECTED routes (one has no account yet, by
// definition):
//
//   POST /register/access     "Create a patient account" button of the
//                             authentication page: checks the captcha of
//                             THAT page, then opens the form
//   GET  /register            the form
//   POST /register            the creation, then back to the login page
//
// The flow is protected against bots by ONE captcha, the one of the
// authentication page:
//   1. the "Create a patient account" button sends the login form
//      to /register/access; if the captcha is typed correctly, the server
//      issues a pass (see auth/registration-pass.service.ts);
//   2. without a valid pass, /register sends back to the
//      authentication page - typing the URL directly is useless;
//   3. the pass is consumed on creation: one solved captcha
//      allows creating ONE account;
//   4. in addition, the number of accounts created per hour and per IP address is
//      limited (see auth/attempt-limiter.service.ts).
//
// The account created is exactly the one the ADMIN would create from the
// "Clients" page (same business layer method: addClient), except
// that the patient CHOOSES their login and password (required, with
// confirmation).
// =========================================================================

import { Body, Controller, Get, HttpCode, Post, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { ApplicationModelService } from '../application-model.service';
import { CaptchaService } from '../../auth/captcha.service';
import { AttemptLimiterService } from '../../auth/attempt-limiter.service';
import { COOKIE_REGISTRATION_PASS, RegistrationPassService } from '../../auth/registration-pass.service';
import { BusinessException } from '../../business/business.exception';
import { flash } from '../view-context';
import {
  BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS,
  FormErrors,
  invalidFields,
  titleOptions,
  validateForm,
} from '../helpers/form.helper';
import { RegistrationFormDto, PASSWORD_MIN } from '../models/person-form.dto';

interface RegistrationValues {
  title: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  login: string;
}

@Controller('register')
export class RegistrationController {
  constructor(
    private readonly application: ApplicationModelService,
    private readonly captchaService: CaptchaService,
    private readonly limiter: AttemptLimiterService,
    private readonly passes: RegistrationPassService,
  ) {}

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /register/access   fields: captchaId, captcha (those of the
  // authentication page; login and password, also sent, are ignored)
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post('access')
  access(@Body() body: Record<string, unknown>, @Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response): void {
    const ip = req.ip ?? 'unknown';

    // too many accounts created recently from this address: no point going further
    const minutes = this.limiter.registrationBlockMinutes(ip);
    if (minutes > 0) {
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS', params: { minutes: String(minutes) } });
      return res.redirect('/login');
    }

    // captcha missing or wrong: back to the authentication page, with
    // a new image (a failure counts as a login failure)
    if (!this.captchaService.verify(body.captchaId, body.captcha)) {
      this.limiter.loginFailure(ip, '');
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT' });
      return res.redirect('/login');
    }

    // correct captcha: we issue the pass and open the form
    res.cookie(COOKIE_REGISTRATION_PASS, this.passes.issue(), this.passes.cookieOptions());
    res.redirect('/register');
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /register
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Get()
  form(@Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response): void {
    if (!this.hasPass(req, res)) {
      return;
    }
    this.show(res, { title: 'Mr', firstName: '', lastName: '', login: '' });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /register
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post()
  @HttpCode(200) // if the form is displayed again (see auth.controller.ts)
  async create(@Body() body: Record<string, unknown>, @Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.hasPass(req, res)) {
      return;
    }
    const ip = req.ip ?? 'unknown';
    const { dto, errors } = await validateForm(RegistrationFormDto, body);
    const values: RegistrationValues = {
      title: dto.title ?? 'Mr',
      firstName: typeof dto.firstName === 'string' ? dto.firstName : '',
      lastName: typeof dto.lastName === 'string' ? dto.lastName : '',
      login: dto.login ?? '',
    };

    // 1. too many accounts created recently from this address?
    const minutes = this.limiter.registrationBlockMinutes(ip);
    if (minutes > 0) {
      return this.show(res, values, {}, 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS', [], { minutes: String(minutes) });
    }

    // 2. all the input errors at once (fields + confirmation):
    //    the user corrects them all in one go
    const allErrors: FormErrors = { ...(errors ?? {}) };
    if (!allErrors.password && !allErrors.confirmation && dto.password !== dto.confirmation) {
      allErrors.confirmation = 'ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER';
    }
    if (Object.keys(allErrors).length > 0) {
      return this.show(res, values, allErrors);
    }

    // 3. the creation (client + USER account, in a transaction)
    try {
      await this.application.addClient({
        title: dto.title,
        lastName: dto.lastName,
        firstName: dto.firstName,
        login: dto.login,
        password: dto.password,
      });
    } catch (e) {
      if (!(e instanceof BusinessException)) {
        throw e;
      }
      // login or first + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
      return this.show(res, values, {}, e.key, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS[e.key] ?? []);
    }

    // 4. the pass has been used: it will not allow creating a 2nd account
    this.passes.consume(req.cookies?.[COOKIE_REGISTRATION_PASS]);
    res.clearCookie(COOKIE_REGISTRATION_PASS, { path: '/register' });
    this.limiter.registrationSuccess(ip);

    // 5. back to the login page, login pre-filled
    flash(res, { type: 'success', key: 'REGISTRATION.DONE', params: { login: dto.login } });
    res.redirect(`/login?${new URLSearchParams({ login: dto.login }).toString()}`);
  }

  // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

  // no valid pass: back to the authentication page
  private hasPass(req: Request, res: Response): boolean {
    if (this.passes.isValid(req.cookies?.[COOKIE_REGISTRATION_PASS])) {
      return true;
    }
    flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT' });
    res.redirect('/login');
    return false;
  }

  // the form; never any password sent back to the browser
  private show(
    res: Response,
    values: RegistrationValues,
    errors: FormErrors = {},
    error: string | null = null,
    otherFields: string[] = [],
    errorParams?: Record<string, string>,
  ): void {
    res.render('account/registration', {
      pageTitle: 'REGISTRATION.TITLE',
      values,
      titles: titleOptions(values.title),
      errors,
      invalidFields: invalidFields(errors, otherFields),
      error: error ?? (Object.keys(errors).length > 0 ? 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM' : null),
      errorParams,
      passwordMin: PASSWORD_MIN,
    });
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 69–91: The “Create a patient account” button on the login page sends the login form to this address (attribute [formaction]; see Example 20). The page’s CAPTCHA is verified; if it’s correct, a pass is stored in a cookie and the browser is redirected to the form;
  • lines 96–102: the form, but only with a valid pass;
  • lines 109–163: account creation: pass, time limit, validation (including verification that the password matches its confirmation), creation by the business layer. The pass is then consumed, and the patient is redirected to the login page with their username pre-filled;
  • lines 168–175: without a pass, return to the login page with a message;
  • lines 178–185: the form. [passwordMin] is used for the help text (“At least 6 characters”).
