docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/controllers/patient-area.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The PERSONAL pages of the patient (USER role), the one they see right
// after logging in:
//
//   GET  /my-area                  home page: [Manage my account],
//                                  [View a schedule], and the upcoming appointment
//   POST /my-area/cancel           cancels THEIR appointment
//   GET  /my-account               form to edit their account
//   POST /my-account               update
//   POST /my-account/delete        deletion of the account (and of its appointments)
//
// Golden rule of this controller: the patient concerned is ALWAYS the one of the
// token (connectedPatient), never an identifier sent by the browser.
// A patient therefore can neither see, nor edit, nor cancel what belongs
// to another patient, even by crafting their own requests.
//
// Any update or deletion of the account requires the CURRENT
// password: someone who found a session left open could
// neither change the password nor delete the account. Current password
// errors are counted as login failures (same limit).
// =========================================================================

import { Body, Controller, Get, HttpCode, Post, Render, Req, Res, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { ApplicationModelService } from '../application-model.service';
import { AuthService } from '../../auth/auth.service';
import { AttemptLimiterService } from '../../auth/attempt-limiter.service';
import { JwtAuthGuard } from '../../auth/jwt-auth.guard';
import { RolesGuard } from '../../auth/roles.guard';
import { Roles } from '../../auth/roles.decorator';
import { ConnectedUser } from '../../auth/jwt.strategy';
import { COOKIE_JWT, jwtCookieOptions } from '../../auth/auth.constants';
import { BusinessException } from '../../business/business.exception';
import { Client } from '../../entities/client.entity';
import { flash } from '../view-context';
import { formatTime, formatDay } from '../helpers/dates.helper';
import { label, connectedPatient } from '../helpers/patient.helper';
import {
  BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS,
  FormErrors,
  invalidFields,
  titleOptions,
  validateForm,
} from '../helpers/form.helper';
import { MyAccountFormDto, PASSWORD_MIN } from '../models/person-form.dto';

type AuthenticatedRequest = Request & { user: ConnectedUser };

interface MyAccountValues {
  title: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  login: string;
  version: number | null;
}

@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard)
@Roles('USER')
@Controller()
export class PatientAreaController {
  constructor(
    private readonly application: ApplicationModelService,
    private readonly authService: AuthService,
    private readonly limiter: AttemptLimiterService,
  ) {}

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /my-area
  // @Res({ passthrough: true }): we access the response (to read the language
  // in res.locals) WITHOUT giving up the normal operation of @Render.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Get('my-area')
  @Render('patient/area')
  async area(@Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest, @Res({ passthrough: true }) res: Response) {
    const patient = await connectedPatient(this.application, req.user);
    const appointments = await this.application.getClientUpcomingAppointments(patient.id);
    return {
      pageTitle: 'AREA.TITLE',
      patient: label(patient),
      appointments: appointments.map((appointment) => ({
        id: appointment.id,
        day: formatDay(appointment.day, res.locals.lang),
        time: `${formatTime(appointment.slot.startHour, appointment.slot.startMinute)} - ${formatTime(appointment.slot.endHour, appointment.slot.endMinute)}`,
        doctor: label(appointment.slot.doctor),
        // link to the doctor's schedule on that day: the patient sees their name there
        scheduleUrl: `/schedule?${new URLSearchParams({ doctorId: String(appointment.slot.doctor.id), day: appointment.day })}`,
      })),
    };
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /my-area/cancel   field: appointmentId
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post('my-area/cancel')
  async cancelAppointment(
    @Body() body: Record<string, string>,
    @Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const patient = await connectedPatient(this.application, req.user);
    const appointment = await this.application.getAppointmentById(Number(body.appointmentId) || 0);
    // an appointment that does not exist, and one of ANOTHER patient, get
    // the same answer: nothing is revealed about other people's appointments
    if (appointment === null || appointment.clientId !== patient.id) {
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: 'ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND' });
    } else {
      await this.application.deleteAppointment(appointment);
      flash(res, { type: 'success', key: 'SCHEDULE.CANCELLED' });
    }
    res.redirect('/my-area');
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /my-account
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Get('my-account')
  async accountForm(@Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest, @Res() res: Response): Promise<void> {
    const patient = await connectedPatient(this.application, req.user);
    this.show(res, {
      title: patient.title,
      firstName: patient.firstName,
      lastName: patient.lastName,
      login: patient.user.login,
      version: patient.version,
    });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /my-account
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post('my-account')
  @HttpCode(200) // if the form is displayed again (see auth.controller.ts)
  async editAccount(
    @Body() body: Record<string, unknown>,
    @Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const patient = await connectedPatient(this.application, req.user);
    const { dto, errors } = await validateForm(MyAccountFormDto, body);
    const values: MyAccountValues = {
      title: dto.title ?? patient.title,
      firstName: typeof dto.firstName === 'string' ? dto.firstName : '',
      lastName: typeof dto.lastName === 'string' ? dto.lastName : '',
      login: dto.login ?? '',
      version: dto.version ?? null,
    };

    const allErrors: FormErrors = { ...(errors ?? {}) };
    if (!allErrors.password && dto.password !== undefined && dto.password !== dto.confirmation) {
      allErrors.confirmation = 'ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER';
    }
    if (Object.keys(allErrors).length > 0) {
      return this.show(res, values, allErrors);
    }

    // the current password
    const passwordError = await this.checkCurrentPassword(req, patient, dto.currentPassword);
    if (passwordError !== null) {
      return this.show(
        res,
        values,
        passwordError.key === 'ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD' ? { currentPassword: passwordError.key } : {},
        passwordError.key,
        [],
        passwordError.params,
      );
    }

    try {
      const client = await this.application.editClient(patient.id, {
        title: dto.title,
        lastName: dto.lastName,
        firstName: dto.firstName,
        login: dto.login,
        password: dto.password, // undefined = unchanged
        version: dto.version,
      });
      // the login and the display name are IN the token: we issue a
      // new one, otherwise the navigation bar would keep the old name
      res.cookie(COOKIE_JWT, this.authService.createToken(client.user), jwtCookieOptions());
      flash(res, { type: 'success', key: 'MY_ACCOUNT.UPDATED' });
      res.redirect('/my-area');
    } catch (e) {
      if (!(e instanceof BusinessException)) {
        throw e;
      }
      this.show(res, values, {}, e.key, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS[e.key] ?? []);
    }
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // POST /my-account/delete   field: deletePassword
  // The account, the client and ALL their appointments disappear together,
  // then the patient is logged out.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  @Post('my-account/delete')
  async deleteAccount(
    @Body() body: Record<string, string>,
    @Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const patient = await connectedPatient(this.application, req.user);
    const passwordError = await this.checkCurrentPassword(req, patient, body.deletePassword);
    if (passwordError !== null) {
      flash(res, { type: 'danger', key: passwordError.key, params: passwordError.params });
      return res.redirect('/my-account');
    }
    await this.application.deleteClient(patient.id);
    res.clearCookie(COOKIE_JWT, { path: '/' });
    flash(res, { type: 'success', key: 'MY_ACCOUNT.DELETED' });
    res.redirect('/login');
  }

  // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

  // null if the current password is correct; otherwise the key of the message
  private async checkCurrentPassword(
    req: Request,
    patient: Client,
    password: unknown,
  ): Promise<{ key: string; params?: Record<string, string> } | null> {
    const ip = req.ip ?? 'unknown';
    const login = patient.user.login;
    const minutes = this.limiter.loginBlockMinutes(ip, login);
    if (minutes > 0) {
      return { key: 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', params: { minutes: String(minutes) } };
    }
    const ok =
      typeof password === 'string' &&
      password !== '' &&
      (await this.authService.validateUser(login, password)) !== null;
    if (!ok) {
      this.limiter.loginFailure(ip, login);
      return { key: 'ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD' };
    }
    return null;
  }

  private show(
    res: Response,
    values: MyAccountValues,
    errors: FormErrors = {},
    error: string | null = null,
    otherFields: string[] = [],
    errorParams?: Record<string, string>,
  ): void {
    res.render('patient/account', {
      pageTitle: 'MY_ACCOUNT.TITLE',
      values,
      titles: titleOptions(values.title),
      errors,
      invalidFields: invalidFields(errors, otherFields),
      error: error ?? (Object.keys(errors).length > 0 ? 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM' : null),
      errorParams,
      passwordMin: PASSWORD_MIN,
    });
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 59–60: reserved for patients;
  • lines 14–17: the golden rule of this controller: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token, never an identifier sent by the browser;
  • lines 74–91: the “My area” page. [@Res({ passthrough: true })] provides access to the response (to read the language in [res.locals] and format the date) without giving up [@Render] (see Example 05);
  • lines 96–101: canceling an appointment. A nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information about other patients’ appointments is disclosed;
  • lines 118–128: the account form, pre-filled;
  • lines 133–139: the update: validation, verification of the current password, then the business logic layer. The token contains the login and the display name: after an update, a new token is issued (line 182); otherwise, the navigation bar would retain the old name;
  • Lines 198–203: Delete the account, the record, and all appointments (using the same business layer method as for ADMIN), then log out;
  • lines 219–223: The current password is required for any changes: someone who finds a session that has been left open would be unable to change the password or delete the account. Errors count as login failures;
  • lines 241–248: the form.

docs.title: 11.15. The Views
docs.text: The views have almost no decisions to make: their template has been prepared by the controllers. Each view begins with a comment [Handlebars] [{{!-- ... --}}] that describes its role; these comments do not appear in the pages sent to the browser.

docs.title: 11.15.1.1. views/layout.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/layout.hbs
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  The template COMMON to all pages. hbs uses it automatically
  (file named "layout.hbs" at the root of the views folder): the page
  requested by the controller (schedule.hbs, login.hbs...) is inserted at
  the {{{body}}} spot.

  Triple braces {{{ }}}: the content is inserted AS IS, without
  escaping - essential here, since [body] is HTML already built.
  Everywhere else we use {{ }}, which escapes the characters < > & " '
  (protection against HTML injection through an entered name, for example).

  Messages: a success is displayed at the TOP of the page ({{> flash}}), an
  error at the BOTTOM, on a light pink background ({{> errors}}).

  Equivalent of src/index.html + app.html of the Angular client.
  ==========================================================================
--}}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="{{lang}}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>{{t pageTitle}} - {{t 'APP.TITLE'}}</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-4">
    {{> navbar}}
    {{> flash}}
    {{{body}}}
    {{> errors}}
  </div>
  {{!-- the "Are you sure?" dialog, hidden as long as it is not needed --}}
  {{> confirmation}}
  <script src="/js/app.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
  • line 22: the page’s language (see Example 22);
  • line 26: the title, translated: the key [pageTitle] is provided by each action;
  • lines 32–35: the navigation bar, the success message, the page, and the error area;
  • lines 38–39: the confirmation window and its script (see Example 21).

docs.title: 11.15.1.2. views/partials/navbar.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  views/partials/navbar.hbs - the navigation bar (inserted by {{> navbar}}).

  Same content as that of the Angular client (title, FR/EN, role, name,
  logout), plus a menu whose entries depend on the role:
  "Doctors" and "Clients" appear only for the ADMIN. It is only a
  display convenience: the real protection is the guards of the
  controllers (a USER who types /doctors by hand gets a 403 page).
  A patient (USER) also has their "My area" menu.
--}}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">{{t 'APP.TITLE'}}</span>

  {{#if currentUser}}
    <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
      {{#if currentUser.isPatient}}
        <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link {{active currentPath '/my-'}}" href="/my-area">{{t 'APP.MENU_MY_AREA'}}</a></li>
      {{/if}}
      <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link {{active currentPath '/schedule'}}" href="/schedule">{{t 'APP.MENU_SCHEDULE'}}</a></li>
      {{#if currentUser.isAdmin}}
        <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link {{active currentPath '/doctors'}}" href="/doctors">{{t 'APP.MENU_DOCTORS'}}</a></li>
        <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link {{active currentPath '/clients'}}" href="/clients">{{t 'APP.MENU_PATIENTS'}}</a></li>
      {{/if}}
    </ul>
  {{else}}
    <div class="me-auto"></div>
  {{/if}}

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {{!-- FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), the active language highlighted --}}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      <a class="btn {{#if (eq lang 'fr')}}btn-light{{else}}btn-outline-light{{/if}}" href="/language/fr">FR</a>
      <a class="btn {{#if (eq lang 'en')}}btn-light{{else}}btn-outline-light{{/if}}" href="/language/en">EN</a>
    </div>

    {{#if currentUser}}
      <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{currentUser.role}}</span>
      <span class="text-white">{{currentUser.name}}</span>
      {{!-- logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button --}}
      <form method="post" action="/logout" class="m-0">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{{t 'APP.LOGOUT'}}</button>
      </form>
    {{/if}}
  </div>
</nav>
  • lines 14–25: the menus depend on the role: “My area” for a patient, “Doctors” and “Patients” for the ADMIN. This is merely for convenience; security is ensured by the controller guards;
  • lines 31–34: the links FR / EN;
  • lines 36–43: the role, name, and logout button in a POST form.

docs.title: 11.15.1.3. views/partials/flash.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  views/partials/flash.hbs - the SUCCESS message set by the previous
  action (appointment booked, doctor added...), displayed only
  once, at the top of the page (see src/web/view-context.ts).
  An ERROR flash message, for its part, is displayed at the bottom of the page, by
  views/partials/errors.hbs.
--}}
{{#if (eq flash.type 'success')}}
  <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">
    {{t flash.key name=flash.params.name login=flash.params.login minutes=flash.params.minutes}}
  </div>
{{/if}}

line 10: the message is a key; its possible parameters ([name], [login], [minutes]) are passed to the helper [t].

docs.title: 11.15.1.4. views/partials/errors.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/partials/errors.hbs - the error zone, at the BOTTOM of each page, on
  a light pink background (.error-zone class, see public/css/styles.css).

  It groups the two possible sources of error:
    - [error]: the error of the displayed page (form refused, login or
      first + last name already used, invalid date, wrong password...);
    - an error flash message, set by the previous action before a
      redirect (slot already booked, deletion refused...).

  role="alert": a screen reader announces the message as soon as
  the page is displayed, even if it is at the bottom.
  ==========================================================================
--}}
{{#if (or error (eq flash.type 'danger'))}}
  <div class="error-zone" role="alert">
    {{#if error}}
      <div>{{t error minutes=errorParams.minutes}}</div>
    {{/if}}
    {{#if (eq flash.type 'danger')}}
      <div>{{t flash.key name=flash.params.name login=flash.params.login minutes=flash.params.minutes}}</div>
    {{/if}}
  </div>
{{/if}}

Line 16: The area is displayed if there is a page error or a flash error message: the helper [or] combines both conditions, with [eq] used as a sub-expression.

docs.title: 11.15.1.5. views/partials/confirmation.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/partials/confirmation.hbs - the "Are you sure?" modal dialog.

  It replaces the browser's window.confirm() box, which can neither be
  styled nor translated (its buttons stay in the language of the
  browser, not in that of the page).

  ONE dialog for the whole page, hidden (d-none) at first. Its
  labels are translated here, by the server, like the rest of the page;
  the small public/js/app.js script merely shows it, puts in it
  the message specific to the form (data-confirmation attribute), and submits
  the form if the user confirms.

  Same Bootstrap classes as the booking dialog (partials/booking.hbs).
  ==========================================================================
--}}
<div id="confirmation-modal" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="confirmation-modal-title" aria-describedby="confirmation-modal-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="confirmation-modal-title">{{t 'CONFIRMATION.TITLE'}}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="no" aria-label="{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA'}}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="confirmation-modal-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {{!-- "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes
               "Cancel this appointment?", and a "Cancel" button would be ambiguous --}}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="no">{{t 'CONFIRMATION.NO'}}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="yes">{{t 'CONFIRMATION.YES'}}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

The window from Example 21, with translated labels and accessibility attributes: [role="alertdialog"], and [aria-labelledby] / [aria-describedby], which specify the title and message read by a screen reader.

docs.title: 11.15.1.6. views/partials/captcha.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/partials/captcha.hbs - the captcha of the authentication page
  (see src/auth/captcha.service.ts). It protects both the login and
  access to account creation ("Create a patient account" button).

  {{{captcha.svg}}}: triple braces, the SVG image is inserted AS IS
  in the page. It is safe here because this SVG is built by the
  server itself (svg-captcha library) and contains nothing that comes
  from the user - we would NEVER do that with user input.

  The hidden captchaId field tells the server WHICH captcha to check; the right
  answer, for its part, is never sent to the browser.
  "Another image" simply reloads the page (path = the current URL).
  ==========================================================================
--}}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{{t 'CAPTCHA.LABEL'}}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{{t 'CAPTCHA.IMAGE_ALT'}}">{{{captcha.svg}}}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{{currentPath}}">{{t 'CAPTCHA.NEW_IMAGE'}}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captchaId" value="{{captcha.id}}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off" spellcheck="false" required
         class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.captcha}}is-invalid{{/if}}">
  {{#if errors.captcha}}
    <div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.captcha}}</div>
  {{else}}
    <div class="form-text">{{t 'CAPTCHA.HELP'}}</div>
  {{/if}}
</div>
  • line 20: the image SVG, inserted as-is (triple curly braces): it is generated by the server, with no user input;
  • line 21: “Another image” simply reloads the page;
  • line 23: the CAPTCHA ID, in a hidden field.

docs.title: 11.15.1.7. views/partials/personFields.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  views/partials/personFields.hbs - the identity fields (title, first name,
  last name), common to three forms: the ADMIN's doctor/client form,
  "Create a patient account" and "Manage my account".
  The partial uses the model of the page that inserts it: values, titles,
  errors (message under the field) and invalidFields (red frame).
--}}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="title">{{t 'PERSONS.TITLE_LABEL'}}</label>
  <select id="title" name="title" class="form-select {{#if invalidFields.title}}is-invalid{{/if}}">
    {{#each titles}}
      <option value="{{value}}" {{#if selected}}selected{{/if}}>{{value}}</option>
    {{/each}}
  </select>
  {{#if errors.title}}<div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.title}}</div>{{/if}}
</div>

<div class="row g-3 mb-3">
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="firstName">{{t 'PERSONS.FIRSTNAME_LABEL'}}</label>
    <input id="firstName" name="firstName" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.firstName}}is-invalid{{/if}}" value="{{values.firstName}}">
    {{#if errors.firstName}}<div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.firstName}}</div>{{/if}}
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="lastName">{{t 'PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL'}}</label>
    <input id="lastName" name="lastName" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.lastName}}is-invalid{{/if}}" value="{{values.lastName}}">
    {{#if errors.lastName}}<div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.lastName}}</div>{{/if}}
  </div>
</div>

The identity fields, common to three forms (see Example 19). A partial inserted without parameters uses the template of the page that inserts it: [values], [titles], [errors], [invalidFields].

docs.title: 11.15.1.8. views/partials/booking.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/partials/booking.hbs - the booking dialog.

  Same technique as the Angular client (booking-dialog): the REAL Bootstrap
  classes of a modal dialog (.modal, .modal-backdrop...), made
  visible "hard-coded" (show d-block) rather than by Bootstrap's
  JavaScript. The difference: it is the SERVER that decides to display it
  (&book=... parameter of the URL), and closing it amounts to following a link
  to the same page without this parameter.
  ==========================================================================
--}}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="booking-title">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="/schedule/book" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="booking-title">{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE'}}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{backUrl}}" aria-label="{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA'}}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT' time=booking.time}}</p>

        {{!-- what the server needs to know in addition to the chosen patient --}}
        <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{doctorId}}">
        <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{day}}">
        <input type="hidden" name="slotId" value="{{booking.slotId}}">

        {{#if booking.patient}}
          {{!-- a patient books for themselves: no list to choose from
               (and the server ignores any clientId anyway) --}}
          <p class="mb-0">{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL'}}: <strong>{{booking.patient}}</strong></p>
        {{else}}
          <label class="form-label" for="clientId">{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL'}}</label>
          <select id="clientId" name="clientId" class="form-select" required autofocus>
            <option value="">{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT'}}</option>
            {{#each booking.clients}}
              <option value="{{id}}">{{label}}</option>
            {{/each}}
          </select>
        {{/if}}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{backUrl}}">{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL'}}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{t 'BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM'}}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>
  • lines 13–14: the [Bootstrap] classes of a modal window, made visible “hard-coded”: the server decides to display it;
  • line 19: closing the window means following a link to the same page, without the [book] parameter;
  • lines 26–28: the form’s hidden fields;
  • lines 30–34: a patient sees their name; an administrator selects the patient from a list.

docs.title: 11.15.2.1. views/login.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/login.hbs - the login form.
  Equivalent of features/login/ of the Angular client. An ordinary HTML <form>:
  the browser itself sends login, password and captcha answer with
  POST /login, without JavaScript. On failure, the server sends back THIS
  page, with the login already entered, a NEW captcha and [error], displayed
  at the bottom of the page by the layout.
  ==========================================================================
--}}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{t 'LOGIN.TITLE'}}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="/login">
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{t 'LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL'}}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="{{login}}" required {{#unless login}}autofocus{{/unless}}>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{{t 'LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL'}}</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required {{#if login}}autofocus{{/if}}>
        </div>

        {{> captcha}}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{t 'LOGIN.SUBMIT'}}</button>

        {{!-- no account yet: a patient can create one themselves.
             It is NOT a simple link: it is a second submit button of
             THIS form, which goes to another address (formaction). The
             server checks the captcha above there before opening the
             account creation page (see RegistrationController).
             formnovalidate: the browser does not require login and password
             (useless to create an account); it is the server that checks
             the captcha. Enter in a field always triggers the FIRST
             button of the form, "Log in". --}}
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="/register/access" formnovalidate>{{t 'LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT'}}</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">{{t 'LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT_HELP'}}</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        {{t 'LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS'}}
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - {{t 'LOGIN.DEMO_ADMIN'}}</li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - {{t 'LOGIN.DEMO_DOCTOR'}}</li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - {{t 'LOGIN.DEMO_USER'}}</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 20: the cursor is placed in the login field, or in the password field if the login is already known;
  • line 28: the CAPTCHA;
  • lines 41–42: the second button submits the same form to [/register/access] ([formaction]). [formnovalidate]: the browser does not require a username and password, as they are not needed to create an account.

docs.title: 11.15.2.2. views/schedule.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/schedule.hbs - the main page (see ScheduleController).
  Three blocks, like the three components of the Angular client:
    1. the choice of the doctor and the day   (<app-doctor-day-picker>)
    2. the schedule                           (<app-agenda>)
    3. the booking dialog                     (<app-booking-dialog>)
  ==========================================================================
--}}

{{!-- a possible error (invalid date, unknown doctor) is displayed
     at the bottom of the page by the layout (see views/partials/errors.hbs) --}}

{{!-- 1. choice of the doctor and the day: a GET form, which simply
     reloads this page with ?doctorId=...&day=... in the URL --}}
<form method="get" action="/schedule" class="card p-3 mb-3">
  <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
    <div class="col-sm-5">
      <label class="form-label" for="doctorId">{{t 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DOCTOR_LABEL'}}</label>
      <select id="doctorId" name="doctorId" class="form-select" required>
        <option value="">{{t 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.CHOOSE_DOCTOR'}}</option>
        {{#each doctors}}
          <option value="{{id}}" {{#if selected}}selected{{/if}}>{{label}}</option>
        {{/each}}
      </select>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-4">
      <label class="form-label" for="day">{{t 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DAY_LABEL'}}</label>
      <input id="day" name="day" type="date" class="form-control" value="{{day}}" required>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-3">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{t 'DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.VIEW_SCHEDULE'}}</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</form>

{{!-- patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no "Book" button --}}
{{#if info}}
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    {{t info}} <a href="/my-area" class="alert-link">{{t 'APP.MENU_MY_AREA'}}</a>
  </div>
{{/if}}

{{!-- 2. the schedule --}}
{{#if schedule}}
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{{t 'SCHEDULE.TITLE_PREFIX'}} {{schedule.day}} - {{schedule.doctor}}</h5>

    {{#if schedule.rows.length}}
      <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>{{t 'SCHEDULE.COLUMN_SLOT'}}</th>
            <th>{{t 'SCHEDULE.COLUMN_STATUS'}}</th>
            <th></th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {{#each schedule.rows}}
            <tr {{#if bookable}}class="free-slot"{{/if}}>
              <td>{{time}}</td>
              <td>
                {{!-- [patient] is set only if the user is allowed
                     to see this name (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient for THEIR
                     appointment) - otherwise, simply "Booked" --}}
                {{#if free}}
                  <span class="badge text-bg-success">{{t 'SCHEDULE.FREE'}}</span>
                {{else if patient}}
                  <span class="badge {{#if mine}}text-bg-primary{{else}}text-bg-secondary{{/if}}">{{patient}}</span>
                {{else}}
                  <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{{t 'SCHEDULE.BOOKED_BY_OTHER'}}</span>
                {{/if}}
              </td>
              <td>
                {{!-- the buttons displayed were decided by the controller
                     (bookable, appointmentId) according to the user's role --}}
                {{#if bookable}}
                  {{!-- "Book" is a simple link: it reopens this page
                       with the booking dialog of this slot --}}
                  <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="{{bookUrl}}">{{t 'SCHEDULE.BOOK'}}</a>
                {{/if}}
                {{#if appointmentId}}
                  {{!-- "Cancel" CHANGES data: so it is a POST.
                       @root: the model of the PAGE (inside an {{#each}},
                       plain names refer to the fields of the current row) --}}
                  <form method="post" action="/schedule/cancel" class="m-0"
                        data-confirmation="{{t 'SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM'}}">
                    <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="{{appointmentId}}">
                    <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{@root.doctorId}}">
                    <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{@root.day}}">
                    <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{{t 'SCHEDULE.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT'}}</button>
                  </form>
                {{/if}}
              </td>
            </tr>
          {{/each}}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    {{else}}
      <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{t 'SCHEDULE.NO_SLOTS'}}</p>
    {{/if}}
  </div>
{{else}}
  <p class="text-muted">{{t 'SCHEDULE.EMPTY_STATE'}}</p>
{{/if}}

{{!-- 3. the booking dialog, only if the URL contains &book=... --}}
{{#if booking}}
  {{> booking}}
{{/if}}
  • Lines 16–35: Selecting a doctor and a date: a form GET (see Example 17). A field [type="date"] sends the date in the format [yyyy-mm-dd];
  • Lines 38–42: A message from a patient who already has an appointment;
  • lines 59–96: one line per time slot. [{{else if patient}}] lists the statuses in sequence: available, booked with a visible name, booked without a name (“Booked”);
  • line 80: “Book” is a link;
  • lines 86–92: “Cancel” is a POST form with confirmation. In the loop, [@root.doctorId] refers to the field in the page template, not the one in the row;
  • lines 108–110: the reservation window, if the controller has prepared it.

docs.title: 11.15.2.4. views/persons/form.hbs
docs.text:
{{!--
  ==========================================================================
  views/persons/form.hbs - creation OR update of a doctor
  or a client (ADMIN). [creating] distinguishes the two cases.

  When the input is refused (empty field, login already taken...), the
  controller sends back THIS view with:
    - the values already entered (values.xxx);
    - the faulty fields framed in red (invalidFields.xxx, Bootstrap
      class "is-invalid");
    - under a field refused by validation, its message (errors.xxx);
    - the error message of the page (error), displayed AT THE BOTTOM of the page
      by the layout (see views/partials/errors.hbs).
  ==========================================================================
--}}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{t pageTitle}}</h5>

      {{!-- novalidate: we let the SERVER validate (it is the one that
           has the final say); the browser checks (required...) are only a
           convenience, which a user can always get around --}}
      <form method="post" action="{{action}}" novalidate>
        {{#unless creating}}
          <input type="hidden" name="version" value="{{values.version}}">
        {{/unless}}

        {{!-- title, first name, last name: partial common to three forms --}}
        {{> personFields}}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{t 'PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION'}}</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{t 'PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL'}}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="off"
                 class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.login}}is-invalid{{/if}}" value="{{values.login}}">
          {{#if errors.login}}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.login}}</div>
          {{else}}
            <div class="form-text">{{#if creating}}{{t 'PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_CREATE'}}{{else}}{{t 'PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_EDIT'}}{{/if}}</div>
          {{/if}}
        </div>

        <div class="mb-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{{t 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_LABEL'}}</label>
          {{!-- never pre-filled: the password never goes back to the browser --}}
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                 class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.password}}is-invalid{{/if}}">
          {{#if errors.password}}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.password}}</div>
          {{else}}
            <div class="form-text">{{#if creating}}{{t 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_CREATE'}}{{else}}{{t 'PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT'}}{{/if}}</div>
          {{/if}}
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{t 'PERSONS.SAVE'}}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{listUrl}}">{{t 'PERSONS.BACK'}}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

  • Lines 25–27: the version number, for a modification;
  • line 30: the identity fields;
  • lines 35–42: the login, with a help text or error message;
  • lines 46–54: the password, which is never pre-filled.

{{!--

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{t 'PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL'}}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="username" required
                 class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.login}}is-invalid{{/if}}" value="{{values.login}}">
          {{#if errors.login}}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.login}}</div>
          {{else}}
            <div class="form-text">{{t 'REGISTRATION.LOGIN_HELP'}}</div>
          {{/if}}

        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">

                   class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.password}}is-invalid{{/if}}">
            {{#if errors.password}}
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.password min=passwordMin}}</div>
            {{else}}
              <div class="form-text">{{t 'REGISTRATION.PASSWORD_HELP' min=passwordMin}}</div>
            {{/if}}
          </div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">{{t 'ACCOUNT.CONFIRMATION_LABEL'}}</label>
            <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password" required
                   class="form-control {{#if invalidFields.confirmation}}is-invalid{{/if}}">
            {{#if errors.confirmation}}<div class="invalid-feedback">{{t errors.confirmation}}</div>{{/if}}
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{t 'REGISTRATION.SUBMIT'}}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="/login">{{t 'REGISTRATION.BACK_TO_LOGIN'}}</a>

docs.title: 11.17.2. public/js/app.js
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// public/js/app.js - the ONLY JavaScript of the application.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The whole application works without JavaScript. This script adds a
// convenience: before sending a form that carries the attribute
// data-confirmation="...", a modal dialog asks "Are you sure?"
// (the dialog itself is in the page: views/partials/confirmation.hbs).
// If JavaScript is disabled, the form is simply sent without
// confirmation - nothing breaks ("progressive enhancement" principle).
//
// Why not window.confirm()? Its box cannot be styled, and its
// buttons stay in the language of the browser, not in that of the page.
// =========================================================================

(() => {
  const modal = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal');
  if (!modal) {
    return;
  }
  const message = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal-message');
  const noButton = modal.querySelector('.modal-footer [data-action="no"]');

  let pendingForm = null; // the form to send if the user confirms
  let previousFocus = null; // the element to give the focus back to on closing

  function open(form) {
    pendingForm = form;
    previousFocus = document.activeElement;
    // textContent (and not innerHTML): the message is displayed as TEXT,
    // never interpreted as HTML
    message.textContent = form.dataset.confirmation;
    modal.classList.remove('d-none');
    // the focus goes on "No": an absent-minded press on Enter deletes nothing
    noButton.focus();
  }

  function close() {
    modal.classList.add('d-none');
    pendingForm = null;
    if (previousFocus) {
      previousFocus.focus();
    }
  }

  // 1. we intercept the sending of the forms to confirm
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((form) => {
    form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
      open(form);
    });
  });

  // 2. the buttons of the dialog (Yes / No / close cross)
  modal.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
    const action = event.target.closest('[data-action]')?.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'yes') {
      const form = pendingForm;
      close();
      // form.submit() sends the form WITHOUT triggering the
      // 'submit' event again: no new confirmation request
      form.submit();
    } else if (action === 'no') {
      close();
    } else if (event.target.classList.contains('modal')) {
      close(); // click on the grey background, outside the dialog
    }
  });

  // 3. keyboard: Escape closes the dialog; Tab stays INSIDE the dialog
  //    (otherwise the focus would go to the greyed-out page, behind)
  modal.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      close();
    } else if (event.key === 'Tab') {
      const buttons = [...modal.querySelectorAll('button')];
      const first = buttons[0];
      const last = buttons[buttons.length - 1];
      if (event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {
        event.preventDefault();
        last.focus();
      } else if (!event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {
        event.preventDefault();
        first.focus();
      }
    }
  });
})();

The completed script for the confirmation window in Example 21:

  • lines 17–19: a page without a confirmation window has nothing to do;
  • line 24: the element that had keyboard focus before the window opened, to which focus is returned when the window closes;
  • lines 26–35: focus is placed on “No, go back”; an accidental press of Enter does not delete anything;
  • lines 37–43: the window is hidden, and focus is restored;
  • Lines 54–67: “Yes,” “No,” the close button, and clicking outside the window. [closest('[data-action]')] finds the element containing the attribute, even if you clicked on an element within it;
  • lines 71–86: The Esc key closes the window; the Tab key cycles the focus within the window, rather than letting it move to the grayed-out page behind it.

docs.title: 12. Conclusion
docs.text:
This document has presented the construction of a MVC web application using the [NestJS] framework: an application whose HTML pages are generated by the server, without a browser-side [JavaScript] framework. It followed the progression of the “Introduction to ASP.NET MVC” course through examples: controllers and routing to views, forms, internationalization, security, and data access, followed by a complete case study.

There are numerous parallels between the two frameworks:

ASP.NET MVC (2013)NestJS (2026)controller, action ([ActionResult])controller [@Controller], action [@Get], [@Post]action template, [[Required]], [[Range]]...Class DTO, decorators of [class-validator][ModelState.IsValid][validate()] and form redispatchviews [Razor] ([.cshtml]), [_Layout.cshtml]views [Handlebars] ([.hbs]), [layout.hbs]partial views, helpers HTMLPartials [{{> name}}], helpers [hbs.registerHelper][TempData]Flash message in a cookiesessioncookies (token JWT, language): stateless serveraction filters, [[Authorize]]middleware, guards ([@UseGuards], [@Roles]), interceptorsresource files ([.resx])dictionaries JSON, helper [t][Entity Framework][TypeORM]

The case study shows that a classic HTML application, without the essential [JavaScript], remains a simple and robust solution: each page is a URL, the browser’s “Back” button works, and the server controls everything. The minimal use of [JavaScript] (the confirmation window) enhances the user experience without being necessary for the application to function.

To learn more, you can consult the [NestJS] documentation (docs.nestjs.com), and compare this application to its two sister applications, which use the same [NestJS] server in version JSON with a [Angular] or [Flutter] client.

docs.title: 2. Controllers, Actions, Routing
docs.text: This chapter examines the path a request takes, from the browser to the action that processes it, and the response that action returns. Views will not be introduced until Chapter 4: here, actions return text or JSON directly.

docs.title: 2.1. Example 01: The Structure of a NestJS Application
docs.text:
The first example is the smallest possible [NestJS] application. It has three files:

01-structure/
├── src/
│   ├── app.controller.ts
│   ├── app.module.ts
│   └── main.ts
├── nest-cli.json
└── tsconfig.json

docs.title: 2.1.1. The entry point: main.ts
docs.text:
import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap() {
  // builds the application from its root module
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
  // starts the HTTP server on port 3000
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Server started on http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 1: [NestFactory] is the “factory” for [NestJS] applications;
  • line 2: the application’s root module, which we’ll cover later;
  • line 4: the startup function is asynchronous ([async]): building the application and starting the server take time, and we wait ([await]) for each step to complete;
  • line 6: builds the application from its root module. [NestJS] then discovers all the application’s controllers and services and creates their instances;
  • line 8: starts the HTTP server on port 3000;
  • line 12: calls the startup function.

docs.title: 2.1.2. The root module: app.module.ts
docs.text:
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppController } from './app.controller';

@Module({
  controllers: [AppController],
})
export class AppModule {}
  • Line 4: The [@Module] decorator turns the [AppModule] class into a [NestJS] module. A module groups together controllers and services that belong together. A small application has only one module; a large one has several (see Example 06);
  • line 5: the list of controllers in the module;
  • line 7: the class itself is empty—everything is in the decorator.

docs.title: 2.1.3. The controller: app.controller.ts
docs.text:
import { Controller, Get } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller()
export class AppController {
  @Get()
  home(): string {
    return 'Hello from NestJS!';
  }
}
  • Line 3: The [@Controller()] decorator turns the class into a controller. Without any arguments, its routes start at the root of the site ([/]);
  • Line 5: The [@Get()] decorator associates the [home] method with [GET /] requests. A method decorated in this way is an action;
  • line 7: The value returned by the action is the response sent to the browser.

docs.title: 2.1.4. Execution
docs.text:
In a console opened in the [01-structure] folder, type [npx nest start]:

[Nest] 12654  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:05 PM     LOG [NestFactory] Starting Nest application...
[Nest] 12654  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:05 PM     LOG [InstanceLoader] AppModule dependencies initialized +9ms
[Nest] 12654  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:05 PM     LOG [RoutesResolver] AppController {/}: +4ms
[Nest] 12654  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:05 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/, GET} route +2ms
[Nest] 12654  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:05 PM     LOG [NestApplication] Nest application successfully started +2ms
Server started on http://localhost:3000

[NestJS] displays the routes it found: in this case, only one, [{/, GET}], served by [AppController]. Let’s look up URL and [http://localhost:3000/] using a browser:

then with [curl]. The [-i] option also displays the HTTP headers from the response (we’ll only show a few of them here):

curl -i http://localhost:3000/

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 18

Hello from NestJS!

A string returned by an action is sent with the header [Content-Type: text/html]: the browser interprets it as HTML.

docs.title: 2.2. Example 02: Routing
docs.text:
Routing associates a URL and a method HTTP (GET, POST...) with an action. Example 02 has two controllers:

02-routing/
├── src/
│   ├── app.controller.ts
│   ├── app.module.ts
│   ├── first.controller.ts
│   └── main.ts
├── nest-cli.json
└── tsconfig.json

The file [src/app.module.ts]:

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppController } from './app.controller';
import { FirstController } from './first.controller';

@Module({
  controllers: [AppController, FirstController],
})
export class AppModule {}

Line 6: The module declares its two controllers.

The file [src/app.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller()
export class AppController {
  // GET /
  @Get()
  home(): string {
    return `<h2>Example 02 - routing</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="/first">/first</a></li>
        <li><a href="/first/action01">/first/action01</a></li>
        <li><a href="/first/products/17">/first/products/17</a></li>
        <li><a href="/first/products/17/reviews/3">/first/products/17/reviews/3</a></li>
        <li><a href="/first/files/images/logo.png">/first/files/images/logo.png</a></li>
        <li><a href="/unknown">/unknown</a></li>
      </ul>`;
  }
}

The [home] action (lines 6–17) returns a HTML page that contains links to the actions of the other controller:

The file [src/first.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Param, Post } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller('first')
export class FirstController {
  // GET /first
  @Get()
  index(): string {
    return 'Action [index] of the [first] controller';
  }

  // GET /first/action01
  @Get('action01')
  action01(): string {
    return 'Action [action01] of the [first] controller, GET request';
  }

  // POST /first/action01: same path, another HTTP method
  @Post('action01')
  action01Post(): string {
    return 'Action [action01Post] of the [first] controller, POST request';
  }

  // GET /first/products/17: [:id] is a route parameter
  @Get('products/:id')
  product(@Param('id') id: string): string {
    return `Product no. ${id}`;
  }

  // GET /first/products/17/reviews/3: two route parameters
  @Get('products/:id/reviews/:number')
  review(@Param() params: { id: string; number: string }): string {
    return `Review no. ${params.number} of product no. ${params.id}`;
  }

  // GET /first/files/...: [*] accepts any end of path
  @Get('files/*')
  file(@Param('0') path: string): string {
    return `Requested file: ${path}`;
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 3: [@Controller('first')] sets the prefix common to all routes in the controller: its actions handle URL routes that begin with [/first];
  • lines 6–7: [@Get()] with no arguments: the action [index] handles [GET /first];
  • lines 12–13: the action [action01] processes [GET /first/action01]. URL is the concatenation of the controller prefix and the action path;
  • lines 18–19: the same path, but for the POST method: [@Post] replaces [@Get]. There are also [@Put], [@Delete], [@Patch], [@All]... The method name [TypeScript] ([action01Post]) is arbitrary: only the decorators matter for routing;
  • Lines 24–25: [:id] is a route parameter: this segment of URL can take any value. The [@Param('id')] decorator injects its value into the action’s [id] parameter. This value is always a string: for [/first/products/17], [id] is ['17'], not the number 17;
  • lines 30–31: two route parameters. [@Param()] without an argument injects an object that contains them all: [{ id: '17', number: '3' }];
  • lines 36–37: the character [*] accepts any ending of URL, including [/]. The corresponding part is the parameter named [0].

Upon startup, [NestJS] displays all routes:

[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [NestFactory] Starting Nest application...
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [InstanceLoader] AppModule dependencies initialized +17ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RoutesResolver] AppController {/}: +8ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/, GET} route +7ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RoutesResolver] FirstController {/first}: +0ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/first, GET} route +1ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/first/action01, GET} route +0ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/first/action01, POST} route +1ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/first/products/:id, GET} route +0ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/first/products/:id/reviews/:number, GET} route +1ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/first/files/*, GET} route +1ms
[Nest] 12690  - 09/23/2026, 4:02:10 PM     LOG [NestApplication] Nest application successfully started +2ms
Server started on http://localhost:3000

Here are the responses to a few queries:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/first

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 40

Action [index] of the [first] controller

curl -i http://localhost:3000/first/action01

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

Action [action01] of the [first] controller, GET request

curl -i http://localhost:3000/first/products/17

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 14

Product no. 17

curl -i http://localhost:3000/first/products/17/reviews/3

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 30

Review no. 3 of product no. 17

curl -i http://localhost:3000/first/files/images/logo.png

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 31

Requested file: images/logo.png

To send a POST request, use the [-X POST] option of [curl]:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/first/action01

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 61

Action [action01Post] of the [first] controller, POST request

Note the status code 201 Created: this is the code that [NestJS] uses by default to respond to a POST. We’ll see how to change it. Finally, a URL that is not handled by any route produces a 404 error, which [NestJS] maps by default to JSON:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/unknown

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 70

{"message":"Cannot GET /unknown","error":"Not Found","statusCode":404}

Chapter 7 will show how to replace this JSON with a HTML page.

docs.title: 2.3. Example 03: Responses to an Action
docs.text:
What an action returns determines the response HTTP. Example 03 reviews the main cases:

The [src/responses.controller.ts] file:

import { Controller, Get, Header, HttpCode, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller('responses')
export class ResponsesController {
  // a string: sent as is, with the [text/html] type
  @Get('html')
  html(): string {
    return '<h1>Action [html]</h1>';
  }

  // the same string, but announced as plain text
  @Get('text')
  @Header('Content-Type', 'text/plain; charset=utf-8')
  text(): string {
    return '<h1>Action [text]</h1>';
  }

  // an object: serialized to JSON, with the [application/json] type
  @Get('json')
  json(): object {
    return { lastName: 'Martin', firstName: 'Jean', age: 42 };
  }

  // an array: also serialized to JSON
  @Get('array')
  array(): string[] {
    return ['Mme', 'Mlle', 'Mr'];
  }

  // a chosen status code: 201 (Created) instead of 200 (OK)
  @Get('created')
  @HttpCode(201)
  created(): object {
    return { message: 'resource created' };
  }

  // no response: the 204 (No Content) code means "nothing to display"
  @Get('empty')
  @HttpCode(204)
  empty(): void {}

  // an asynchronous method: NestJS waits for the promise to settle
  @Get('promise')
  async promise(): Promise<object> {
    const start = Date.now();
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, 500));
    return { wait: `${Date.now() - start} ms` };
  }

  // an exception: NestJS turns it into an error response
  @Get('error')
  error(): string {
    throw new NotFoundException('This resource does not exist');
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • lines 6–9: a string is sent as-is, with the header [Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8];
  • lines 12–16: the [@Header] decorator sets a response header. Declared as plain text ([text/plain]), the same string is no longer interpreted by the browser;
  • lines 19–22: an object is serialized as JSON, with the header [Content-Type: application/json];
  • lines 25–28: an array is also serialized as JSON;
  • lines 31–35: [@HttpCode(201)] changes the response status code (default 200 for a GET);
  • lines 38–40: the code 204 (No Content) means “no content”: the action returns nothing;
  • lines 43–48: an action can be asynchronous ([async]): in that case, it returns a promise ([Promise]), and [NestJS] waits for it to resolve before responding. This is the case for all actions that query a database;
  • Lines 51–54: An action can trigger an exception. The exceptions for [NestJS] ([NotFoundException], [BadRequestException], [ForbiddenException]...) each carry a status code HTTP (here 404), which [NestJS] uses for its response.

The responses received:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/html

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 22

<h1>Action [html]</h1>

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/text

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 22

<h1>Action [text]</h1>

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 49

{"lastName":"Martin","firstName":"Jean","age":42}

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/array

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 19

["Mme","Mlle","Mr"]

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/created

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 30

{"message":"resource created"}

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/empty

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/promise

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 17

{"wait":"501 ms"}

curl -i http://localhost:3000/responses/error

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 79

{"message":"This resource does not exist","error":"Not Found","statusCode":404}

In a browser, the difference between [text/html] and [text/plain] is visible:

docs.title: 2.4. Example 04: Redirects
docs.text:
An action may respond with a redirect: a 301 or 302 status code and a [Location] header that tells the browser which URL to request next. The browser requests it immediately, without user intervention. Redirects are ubiquitous in a web application: after a successful form submission, after logging in, after changing the language...

The [src/redirects.controller.ts] file:

import { Controller, Get, Param, Redirect } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller()
export class RedirectsController {
  // fixed redirect: the address and the code are known in advance
  @Get('old')
  @Redirect('/new', 301)
  oldPage(): void {}

  @Get('new')
  newPage(): string {
    return 'You are on the [new] page';
  }

  // computed redirect: the returned object replaces the @Redirect() address
  @Get('go/:destination')
  @Redirect()
  go(@Param('destination') destination: string): { url: string } {
    return { url: `/page/${destination}` };
  }

  @Get('page/:name')
  page(@Param('name') name: string): string {
    return `You are on the [${name}] page`;
  }

  // redirect to another site
  @Get('documentation')
  @Redirect('https://docs.nestjs.com')
  documentation(): void {}
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • lines 6–8: [@Redirect('/new', 301)]: a permanent redirect. The 301 code (Moved Permanently) indicates that the page has permanently changed its address; the default code is 302 (Found), a temporary redirect;
  • lines 16–20: a calculated redirect: [@Redirect()] without an argument, and the action returns an object [{ url: ... }] that sets the destination address;
  • lines 28–30: You can redirect to another site.

[curl] shows the redirect without following it:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/old

HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
Location: /new
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 38

Moved Permanently. Redirecting to /new

With the [-L] option, [curl] follows the redirect, just as a browser would. We then see the two successive responses:

curl -i -L http://localhost:3000/old

HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
Location: /new
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

You are on the [new] page

curl -i http://localhost:3000/go/contact

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /page/contact
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 35

Found. Redirecting to /page/contact

In the browser, only the final page is visible; the address bar displays the new URL:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/documentation

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://docs.nestjs.com
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 45

Found. Redirecting to https://docs.nestjs.com

docs.title: 2.5. Example 05: The Request and Response Objects in Express
docs.text:
[NestJS] relies on the web server [Express]. An action can directly access the [Request] and [Response] objects from [Express]. This is sometimes necessary, and we’ll do it in the case study (to set a cookie, for example), but you need to be aware of what you’re losing.

The [src/express.controller.ts] file:

import { Controller, Get, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';

@Controller('express')
export class ExpressController {
  // the Express request: method, URL, headers...
  @Get('request')
  request(@Req() req: Request): object {
    return {
      method: req.method,
      url: req.url,
      path: req.path,
      browser: req.get('user-agent'),
    };
  }

  // the Express response: the action sends the response itself
  @Get('response')
  response(@Res() res: Response): void {
    res.status(200).type('text/plain').send('Response sent by [res.send]');
  }

  // redirect with the Express response
  @Get('redirect')
  redirect(@Res() res: Response): void {
    res.redirect('/express/response');
  }

  // passthrough: we use the response (here for a header), but NestJS
  // still sends the value returned by the action itself
  @Get('passthrough')
  passthrough(@Res({ passthrough: true }) res: Response): string {
    res.setHeader('X-Example', '05-express');
    return 'Response sent by NestJS, with an added header';
  }

  // MISTAKE not to make: @Res() without passthrough, and nothing sent
  @Get('blocked')
  blocked(@Res() res: Response): string {
    return 'This string will never be sent: the browser keeps waiting...';
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 2: the types [Request] and [Response] from [Express];
  • Lines 7–15: [@Req()] injects the request [Express]: method HTTP, URL, path, headers ([req.get(...)])... ;
  • lines 18–21: [@Res()] injects the response [Express]. Note: As soon as an action uses [@Res()], [NestJS] assumes that it is the one sending the response and ignores what it returns. Here, the action sets the status code and type, and sends the body using [res.send];
  • lines 24–27: a 302 redirect performed by [Express] to [res.redirect(url)];
  • lines 31–35: With the [passthrough: true] option, the action uses the response (here to add a header) but lets [NestJS] send what it returns. It’s the best of both worlds;
  • lines 38–41: the mistake to avoid: [@Res()] without [passthrough], and no calls to [res.send], [res.redirect], [res.render].... The returned string is ignored, no response is ever sent, and the browser waits indefinitely.

Responses received:

curl -i -A "Mozilla/5.0 (example)" http://localhost:3000/express/request

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 101

{"method":"GET","url":"/express/request","path":"/express/request","browser":"Mozilla/5.0 (example)"}

(the [-A] option in [curl] sets the [User-Agent] header, which identifies the browser)

curl -i http://localhost:3000/express/response

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 27

Response sent by [res.send]

curl -i http://localhost:3000/express/redirect

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /express/response
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 39

Found. Redirecting to /express/response

curl -i http://localhost:3000/express/passthrough

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Example: 05-express
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 45

Response sent by NestJS, with an added header

For the last action, we limit the wait to 3 seconds using the [-m 3] option:

curl -i -m 3 http://localhost:3000/express/blocked

curl: (28) Operation timed out after 3002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received

In the rest of this document, we will use [@Res()] when an action must choose between several responses of different types (a page or a redirect), and we will ensure that each path in the code sends a response.

docs.title: 2.6. Example 06: Modules, Services, and Dependency Injection
docs.text:
Controllers should not contain application logic; they delegate it to services. Example 06 breaks down a small application into two modules:

06-modules/
├── src/
│   ├── clients/
│   │   ├── clients.controller.ts
│   │   └── clients.module.ts
│   ├── products/
│   │   ├── products.controller.ts
│   │   ├── products.module.ts
│   │   └── products.service.ts
│   ├── app.module.ts
│   └── main.ts
├── nest-cli.json
└── tsconfig.json

docs.title: 2.6.1. The ProductsService service
docs.text:
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';

export interface Product {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  price: number;
}

@Injectable()
export class ProductsService {
  private readonly products: Product[] = [
    { id: 1, name: 'pen', price: 1.5 },
    { id: 2, name: 'notebook', price: 3.2 },
    { id: 3, name: 'eraser', price: 0.8 },
  ];

  findAll(): Product[] {
    return this.products;
  }

  findById(id: number): Product | undefined {
    return this.products.find((p) => p.id === id);
  }
}
  • Lines 3–7: The [Product] interface describes a product;
  • line 9: the decorator [@Injectable()] turns the class into a service (also called a provider): [NestJS] creates a single instance of it, which it provides (injects) to all who need it;
  • lines 11–15: the data, here in memory;
  • lines 17–23: the service’s two methods.

docs.title: 2.6.2. The ProductsController controller
docs.text:
import { Controller, Get, NotFoundException, Param } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Product, ProductsService } from './products.service';

@Controller('products')
export class ProductsController {
  // dependency injection: NestJS provides the ProductsService instance
  constructor(private readonly productsService: ProductsService) {}

  @Get()
  list(): Product[] {
    return this.productsService.findAll();
  }

  @Get(':id')
  oneProduct(@Param('id') id: string): Product {
    const product = this.productsService.findById(Number(id));
    if (!product) {
      throw new NotFoundException(`Product no. ${id} not found`);
    }
    return product;
  }
}
  • line 7: dependency injection. The controller declares in its constructor that it needs a [ProductsService]; [NestJS] provides it with the single instance of the service. The controller never calls [new ProductsService()]. The syntax [private readonly productsService: ProductsService] of [TypeScript] declares both the parameter and the field [this.productsService];
  • Lines 9–12: The action delegates to the service;
  • lines 14–21: [Number(id)] converts the route parameter (a string) into a number. A non-existent product triggers a 404 exception.

docs.title: 2.6.3. The ProductsModule module
docs.text:
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ProductsController } from './products.controller';
import { ProductsService } from './products.service';

@Module({
  controllers: [ProductsController],
  providers: [ProductsService],
  exports: [ProductsService],
})
export class ProductsModule {}
  • line 6: the module’s controller;
  • line 7: the module’s services. Only the services declared here (or imported, see below) can be injected into the module’s classes;
  • line 8: the service is exported: modules that import [ProductsModule] will also be able to have it injected.

})

Line 6: [ClientsModule] imports [ProductsModule] and therefore has access to the services that the latter exports.

The file [src/clients/clients.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ProductsService } from '../products/products.service';

@Controller('clients')
export class ClientsController {
  // a service from ANOTHER module, exported by that module
  constructor(private readonly productsService: ProductsService) {}

  @Get('cart')
  cart(): object {
    const products = this.productsService.findAll();
    const total = products.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.price, 0);
    return { client: 'Jean Martin', items: products.length, total };
  }
}
  • Line 7: [ClientsController] has a service from another module injected into it;
  • lines 9–14: it uses this service to calculate the total of a shopping cart.

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';

@Module({

docs.title: 6. Data Scopes
docs.text:
A web application serves many users at once, and each user makes numerous requests. Data can therefore be shared at three levels, known as its scope:

  • application scope: the data is shared by all users throughout the server’s lifetime (the list of doctors, for example);
  • request scope: the data exists only for the duration of a request (a view’s model);
  • client scope: the data is specific to a user and must persist from one request to the next (the selected language, the logged-in user).

The original course used the [ASP.NET] session for this last scope: a server-side storage space unique to each browser. This document, like the case study, does without it: client-side scope data is stored by the browser in cookies. The server does not store anything between two requests from the same user: it is said to be stateless ([stateless]). This is what makes it possible, for example, to run multiple identical servers behind a load balancer. The trade-off: a cookie is under the user’s control, and the user can read and modify it. Chapter 8 will show how a signed token makes it possible to trust the cookie despite this.

docs.title: 6.1. Example 23: Three Scopes
docs.text:
The file [src/counter.service.ts]:

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';

// APPLICATION scope (the default): a single instance, created at startup and
// shared by ALL the requests of ALL the users
@Injectable()
export class CounterService {
  private total = 0;

  increment(): number {
    return ++this.total;
  }
}

Lines 5–6: By default, a [NestJS] service is a singleton: a single instance, created at startup, shared by all requests. Its [total] field therefore has application scope.

The [src/request.service.ts] file:

import { Injectable, Scope } from '@nestjs/common';

let createdInstances = 0;

// REQUEST scope: a NEW instance for each HTTP request
@Injectable({ scope: Scope.REQUEST })
export class RequestService {
  readonly number = ++createdInstances;
}

Line 6: The [scope: Scope.REQUEST] option requests a new instance for each request. The instance number indicates this. This option is rarely used: it incurs a cost (creating objects for each request), and it propagates—a controller that depends on a request-scope service becomes request-scope itself. [res.locals] is usually sufficient.

The file [src/scopes.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { CounterService } from './counter.service';
import { RequestService } from './request.service';

@Controller()
export class ScopesController {
  constructor(
    private readonly counter: CounterService,
    private readonly request: RequestService,
  ) {}

  @Get()
  scopes(@Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response): void {
    // CLIENT scope: a piece of data kept by the BROWSER (cookie),
    // sent back to the server with each request
    const myVisits = Number(req.cookies?.myVisits ?? 0) + 1;
    res.cookie('myVisits', String(myVisits), { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' });
    res.render('scopes', {
      total: this.counter.increment(),
      instance: this.request.number,
      myVisits,
    });
  }
}
  • lines 8–11: both services are injected;
  • lines 17–18: the client scope: a counter stored in a cookie. The browser sends it back with every request; the action increments it and stores it back;
  • lines 19–23: the three values are passed to the view.

The file [src/main.ts]:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { NestExpressApplication } from '@nestjs/platform-express';
import * as cookieParser from 'cookie-parser';
import { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import { dirname, join } from 'path';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule);
  app.useStaticAssets(join(dirname(require.resolve('bootstrap/package.json')), 'dist'), { prefix: '/bootstrap/' });
  app.setBaseViewsDir(join(__dirname, '..', 'views'));
  app.setViewEngine('hbs');
  app.use(cookieParser());
  // REQUEST scope: res.locals is born and dies with the request
  app.use((req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
    res.locals.start = new Date().toISOString().slice(11, 23);
    next();
  });
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Server started on http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();

lines 15–18: the request scope with [res.locals]: the time the request was received.

The file [views/scopes.hbs]:

  <li>application: {{total}} visit(s) of the site, all browsers combined</li>
  <li>request: instance no. {{instance}} of RequestService, request received at {{start}}</li>
  <li>client: {{myVisits}} visit(s) from this browser</li>
</ul>

docs.title: 5. Internationalization
docs.text: An internationalized application displays its text in the user’s language. The case study is in French and English. The principle is simple: the views no longer contain text, but keys ([MENU.HOME]), and a dictionary for each language associates a text with each key. The selected language is stored in a cookie.

docs.title: 5.1. Example 22: A Bilingual Application
docs.text:
